docs.title: 3.1 2D Modeling Automation
docs.text:
Understand the GUI workflow first, repeat the same operations manually once or twice, and move to remote control when the flow becomes repetitive.

Shared rules (target, scripts, session files, exit codes) live in Remote Control Basics. For section-specific command reference, start with hf2DStudio Remote Control Overview.

docs.title: 3.2.1 hf2DStudio Commands
docs.text:
Typical flow: file → view → geometry → section data → operation/analysis.

Shared rules (target selection, scripts, session files, exit codes) are in Remote Control Basics. If the GUI workflow is new, start with hf2DStudio GUI Guide.

docs.title: 3.3 hf2DStudio Remote Control Window and File
3.3.1 Remote-only
docs.text:
• Use these commands first to identify the running instance and confirm that remote control is working.
hf2DStudio --remote list
hf2DStudio --remote target <set|show|clear> [id]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] status
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] ping
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] focus
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] maximize
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] minimize
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--timeout-ms <ms>] script <file>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] script-save [file]
  • target: manage the local default target used when --target is omitted; see the target subsection below and Remote Control Basics

docs.title: 3.3.1.1 list
docs.text:
• Lists every running hf2DStudio instance.
  • Syntax: list
  • Validation: No positional arguments.
  • Behavior: Each line is uuid | pid | server | startedAt | file. The leading uuid can be pasted directly into target or --target <id>. When there is no running instance, a short message is printed and the command exits with success code 0. This command runs only in the local client and does not send an IPC request to any target.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote list

docs.title: 3.3.1.2 target
docs.text:
• Stores the local default target used when --target is omitted.
  • Syntax: target set <id> target show target clear
  • Validation: set requires exactly one <id> argument, which must be a uuid or server name shown by list. show and clear take no additional arguments. --target cannot be combined with the target command.
  • Behavior: set resolves the id, writes it to the runtime directory, and prints the resulting JSON. show prints the stored default target as JSON and reports whether the instance is still alive. clear removes the stored default target. This command runs only in the local client.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote target set 4e37d050-cda4-4a24-a885-4e0595554802
hf2DStudio --remote target show
hf2DStudio --remote target clear

docs.title: 3.3.1.3 status
docs.text:
• Returns the current status of the target instance as JSON.
  • Syntax: status
  • Validation: No positional arguments. A target instance must exist.
  • Behavior: Returns JSON with uuid, server name, current file path, start time, unsaved-change flag, and similar fields. Does not change section-model data and does not add any line to Remote Control History.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote status

docs.title: 3.3.1.4 ping
docs.text:
• Checks the IPC connectivity to the target instance.
  • Syntax: ping
  • Validation: No positional arguments.
  • Behavior: Returns success when the connection and the round-trip response are healthy. Does not change section-model data and does not add any line to Remote Control History. Use it in automation scripts to quickly confirm that a target window is reachable.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote ping

docs.title: 3.3.1.5 Window State
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] focus
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] maximize
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] minimize
  • focus restores the window if needed, then raises and activates it.
  • maximize switches the target window to the maximized state, then raises and activates it.
  • minimize minimizes the target window.
  • These commands are remote-only UI helpers: they do not change section-model data and they do not append canonical command tails to Remote Control History.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote maximize
hf2DStudio --remote focus
hf2DStudio --remote minimize

docs.title: 3.3.1.6 script
docs.text:
• Runs commands from a script file, one per line, against the target instance.
  • Syntax: script <file>
  • Validation: <file> must exist. Relative paths resolve against the CLI current working directory. Each line must carry only a command tail, without the hf2DStudio --remote prefix. Lines starting with # and empty lines are treated as comments and skipped.
  • Behavior: If any line fails, the command stops with SCRIPT_FAILED and reports the failing line number and the original error code and message. When a line is quit, the command returns the number of executed lines up to that point and the target window closes. --timeout-ms applies to the whole script request, not to individual lines, so give a long timeout for long scripts.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote --timeout-ms 60000 script D:\Work\build-section.txt

docs.title: 3.3.1.7 script-save
docs.text:
• Saves the Remote Control History accumulated by the target instance into a script file.
  • Syntax: script-save [file]
  • Validation: Without [file], the default output path under <sessionRoot>/.hyfeast/ is used. With [file], that path is used; relative paths resolve against the CLI current working directory.
  • Behavior: Writes the default header comment (# One command tail per line (without "hf2DStudio --remote")) followed by the accumulated command tails as UTF-8 text with CRLF line endings. The saved lines match the history shown in the GUI Command panel. The saved file can be replayed directly with the script command.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote script-save D:\Work\section-recipe.txt

docs.title: 3.3.2 File
docs.text:
• Use these commands to create, open, import into, save, or close section models from scripts or batch flows.
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] new [--discard-unsaved]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] open <file>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] import-dxf-geometry <file>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] save [file]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] quit [--discard-unsaved]
  • new:
  • without --discard-unsaved, follow the same save-confirmation flow as GUI File > New
  • Yes: save the current section first; if it has never been saved, open the Save As dialog
  • No: discard unsaved changes and create a new blank section model
  • Cancel: keep the current section open and fail with NEW_FAILED
  • open, quit:
  • if unsaved changes exist and the current file already has a path, auto-save first
  • if unsaved changes exist and there is no current file path, fail with SAVE_PATH_REQUIRED, except for an Untitled model whose only user change is the startup UnitSystem choice
  • import-dxf-geometry <file>:
  • imports supported DXF entities into the active section Geometry
  • uses the same hfStudio DXF importer path for LINE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE, ARC, CIRCLE, ELLIPSE, and SPLINE, then converts the resulting Construction Guide primitives to Line, Arc, Bezier, or Spline curves
  • ignores the final DXF/WCS z coordinate and uses only (x, y) as hf2DStudio Geometry coordinates
  • applies unit scaling only when both DXF $INSUNITS and the active section/global unit are valid; otherwise imports the numeric coordinates without scaling
  • fails when the active section already has a mesh; run make-mesh delete before importing
  • new --discard-unsaved:
  • discards unsaved changes immediately
  • does not show the GUI save confirmation dialog
  • use it only when the caller intentionally wants a non-interactive discard
  • quit --discard-unsaved:
  • discards unsaved changes without auto-save
  • does not show the GUI save confirmation dialog
  • closes the target window immediately after the remote request is accepted
  • save [file]:
  • without [file], save to current file
  • with [file], save there and update the current file path

docs.title: 3.4.1 View
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] fit [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] grid-spacing <get|set> [<value>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] rotate-axes <angle-deg>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] display-axis <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] display-grid <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] display-geometry <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] ortho-mode <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] snap-to-grid <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] snap-to-geometry <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
  • --view is optional; when omitted it targets the active view of the current tab.
  • --view must be active, left, right, or analysis.
  • grid-spacing matches the toolbar grid-spacing spin box.
  • rotate-axes matches the GUI Rotate axes dialog.
  • display-geometry does not support the analysis view; --view analysis is rejected.
  • GUI toolbar toggles (axis/grid/geometry display, ortho, snap) are recorded into Remote Control History with the same commands.

docs.title: 3.4.1.1 grid-spacing
docs.text:
• Gets or sets the toolbar grid spacing.
  • Syntax: grid-spacing get grid-spacing set <value>
  • Validation: set requires one positive finite number.
  • Behavior: In the Section tab it applies to both left/right section views at once. In the Analysis tab it applies to the analysis view. GUI changes from the grid-spacing spin box are also recorded into Remote Control History with the same command.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote grid-spacing set 25
hf2DStudio --remote grid-spacing get

docs.title: 3.4.1.2 rotate-axes
docs.text:
• Sets the axes angle shown by the GUI Rotate axes dialog.
  • Syntax: rotate-axes <angle-deg>
  • Validation: Angle must be a finite number within [-360, 360].
  • Behavior: In the Section tab it applies to both left/right section views at once. In the Analysis tab it applies to the analysis view. GUI changes from the Rotate axes dialog are also recorded into Remote Control History with the same command.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote rotate-axes 90

docs.title: 3.4.1.3 fit
docs.text:
• Fits the target section view to its current contents.
  • Syntax: fit [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
  • Validation: No positional arguments. When --view is omitted, the active view of the current tab is used.
  • Behavior: In the Section tab with --view active or no --view, only the active section view is fitted. With --view left or right, only that side of the Section tab is fitted. In the Analysis tab with --view analysis or no --view, only the analysis view is fitted. Only zoom/pan state changes; section-model data is not modified.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote fit
hf2DStudio --remote fit --view right

docs.title: 3.4.1.4 display-axis / display-grid / display-geometry
docs.text:
• Shows or hides axes, grid, or section geometry in the target view.
  • Syntax: display-axis <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>] display-grid <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>] display-geometry <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
  • Validation: Exactly one <on|off> argument is required. display-geometry does not accept --view analysis.
  • Behavior: Matches the same toolbar toggle in the GUI. display-geometry off does not affect section-mesh display; it hides only the geometry layer.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote display-axis off
hf2DStudio --remote display-grid on --view left
hf2DStudio --remote display-geometry off --view right

docs.title: 3.4.1.5 ortho-mode
docs.text:
• Enables or disables the orthogonal-drawing helper in the target view.
  • Syntax: ortho-mode <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
  • Validation: Exactly one <on|off> argument is required.
  • Behavior: Matches the GUI ortho toggle on the toolbar. When on, mouse drawing is constrained to axis-aligned directions.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote ortho-mode on

docs.title: 3.4.1.6 snap-to-grid / snap-to-geometry
docs.text:
• Enables or disables grid snapping or geometry snapping in the target view.
  • Syntax: snap-to-grid <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>] snap-to-geometry <on|off> [--view <active|left|right|analysis>]
  • Validation: Exactly one <on|off> argument is required.
  • Behavior: Matches the same toolbar toggle in the GUI. The two snap modes are independent and can be on at the same time; geometry snap takes precedence over grid snap when both are on.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote snap-to-grid on
hf2DStudio --remote snap-to-geometry off

docs.title: 3.5.1 Geometry
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-point <yp,zp>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-lines <yp,zp|P<point-id>> <yp,zp|P<point-id>> [<yp,zp|P<point-id>> ...]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-arc <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-bezier2 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-bezier3 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-rbezier2 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> --weights <w1>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-rbezier3 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> --weights <w1,w2>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-spline <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> [<yp,zp> ...]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] generate-circle <radius> <yp> <zp>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] generate-circular-points <radius> <yp> <zp> <start-angle-deg> <count>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] set-seed --curve-ids <id,id,...> --seed <integer>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] auto-seed --curve-ids <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] make-face --material <name> --curve-ids <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] make-rebar --material <name> --point-ids <id,id,...> --diameter <value> [--diameter-right <value>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] move-point <point-id> <yp,zp> [--merge <on|off>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-point <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-curve <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-face <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-rebar <id,id,...>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] select <point|curve|face|rebar> <id,id,...> [--mode <replace|add|remove|toggle>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-selection
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] merge-selected-points
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] detach-selected-points
  • Geometry authoring commands require an editable geometry section.
  • If a mesh already exists, geometry authoring must not proceed until make-mesh delete is run.
  • Coordinate arguments use yp,zp.
  • Quote coordinate tokens when needed, especially for negative values such as "-25,10".
  • Coordinate-based draw commands resolve against the start-section geometry.
  • In draw-lines, a coordinate token creates a separate point, while P<point-id> connects the line to an existing point.
  • When a requested coordinate matches an existing point, the command still creates a new point instead of reusing the existing one.
  • New points are created with matching start/end coordinates, so taper sections start from the same geometry on both sides.
  • move-point targets one existing point id and updates every connected curve consistently.
  • move-point --merge on is the explicit remote-control path for connecting one moved point into existing topology.
  • Direct delete commands record the actual removed ids, so GUI Delete replay does not depend on prior selection reconstruction.
  • select does not require mesh deletion because it does not change geometry.
  • delete-selection requires editable geometry because it removes selected entities.
  • merge-selected-points merges only selected points that are already coincident.
  • detach-selected-points duplicates selected shared points, but blocks points still referenced by existing faces or rebars.

docs.title: 3.5.1.1 Draw Point
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-point <yp,zp>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <yp,zp> is one geometry-point coordinate pair.
  • The command creates exactly one point.
  • The command creates a new point even if another point already exists at the same coordinates.
  • No curve, face, or rebar is created by this command.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-point "0,0"

docs.title: 3.5.1.2 Draw Lines
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-lines <yp,zp|P<point-id>> <yp,zp|P<point-id>> [<yp,zp|P<point-id>> ...]

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide at least two point tokens.
  • A coordinate token <yp,zp> creates a separate point.
  • A point reference token P<point-id> reuses the existing point and connects the new line segment to that topology.
  • Each adjacent pair becomes one line segment.
  • Two points create one line segment, three points create two connected line segments, and so on.
  • Identical consecutive points are rejected.
  • Repeated non-consecutive points are allowed, so a polyline can return to a previous point.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.
  • GUI Remote History records P<point-id> when the drawing interaction chooses connect to existing point, and records coordinates when it chooses create separate point.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-lines "0,0" "300,0" "300,120"
hf2DStudio --remote draw-lines P1 "300,0" P2

docs.title: 3.5.1.3 Draw Arc
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-arc <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide exactly three points.
  • All three points must be distinct.
  • The three points must not be collinear.
  • The command creates one 2D arc using start, middle, and end points.
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-arc "0,0" "150,80" "300,0"

docs.title: 3.5.1.4 Draw Bezier2
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-bezier2 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide exactly three control points.
  • All three points must be distinct.
  • The command creates one quadratic bezier curve.
  • The stored inner weight is w1 = 1.0.
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-bezier2 "0,0" "150,80" "300,0"

docs.title: 3.5.1.5 Draw Bezier3
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-bezier3 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp>

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide exactly four control points.
  • All four points must be distinct.
  • The command creates one cubic bezier curve.
  • The stored inner weights are w1 = 1.0 and w2 = 1.0.
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-bezier3 "0,0" "100,90" "220,90" "320,0"

docs.title: 3.5.1.6 Draw Rational Bezier2
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-rbezier2 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> --weights <w1>

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide exactly three control points and one inner weight.
  • All three points must be distinct.
  • The command creates one rational quadratic bezier curve.
  • --weights <w1> defines the inner control-point weight.
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-rbezier2 "0,0" "150,80" "300,0" --weights "0.70710678"

docs.title: 3.5.1.7 Draw Rational Bezier3
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-rbezier3 <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> --weights <w1,w2>

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide exactly four control points and two inner weights.
  • All four points must be distinct.
  • The command creates one rational cubic bezier curve.
  • --weights <w1,w2> defines the two inner control-point weights.
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-rbezier3 "0,0" "100,90" "220,90" "320,0" --weights "0.85,0.85"

docs.title: 3.5.1.8 Draw Spline
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] draw-spline <yp,zp> <yp,zp> <yp,zp> [<yp,zp> ...]

Arguments and behavior:

  • Provide at least three control points.
  • The command creates one spline curve through the requested points.
  • Repeated coordinates are rejected except for one closing case:
  • if the last point matches the first point, the spline is created as a closed spline
  • The curve seed is initialized from the current section-model default curve seed.
  • Existing matching points are not reused; a new point is created for each requested coordinate.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote draw-spline "0,0" "120,80" "240,40" "240,-40" "0,0"

docs.title: 3.5.1.9 Move Point
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] move-point <point-id> <yp,zp> [--merge <on|off>]

Arguments and behavior:

  • <point-id> is one existing geometry point id.
  • <yp,zp> is the destination coordinate pair for that point.
  • The command updates every connected curve after the point move.
  • The default is no merge.
  • --merge on keeps the moved point id and merges any duplicate destination point into it.
  • --merge off leaves other points untouched, even if another point already exists at the destination.
  • The command succeeds as a no-op when the destination already matches the current point coordinates.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote move-point 12 "250,100" --merge off

docs.title: 3.5.1.10 Make Face
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] make-face --material <name> --curve-ids <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • --material <name> selects one existing section material.
  • --curve-ids <id,id,...> is a non-empty comma-separated curve-id list.
  • If the requested curves already define one exact face, including hole loops, the command creates that face as-is.
  • Otherwise the command resolves bounded cells from the requested curves and creates one face for each new cell it can determine.
  • Shared boundary curves split neighboring cells into separate faces.
  • Extra curves that do not bound any cell are ignored.
  • Already-existing faces with the same resolved curve set are skipped.
  • The command fails only when it cannot resolve any new face from the requested curves.
  • Success JSON always returns faceIds; faceId is also returned when exactly one face is created.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote make-face --material CONC --curve-ids "1,2,3,4"

docs.title: 3.5.1.11 Delete Point
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-point <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <id,id,...> is a comma-separated point-id list.
  • Points are deleted only when they are not referenced by any remaining curve or rebar.
  • Safe ids are deleted; blocked ids are reported in the JSON result.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote delete-point "8,12"

docs.title: 3.5.1.12 Delete Curve
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-curve <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <id,id,...> is a comma-separated curve-id list.
  • Curves are deleted only when they are not referenced by any remaining face.
  • Safe ids are deleted; blocked ids are reported in the JSON result.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote delete-curve "3,7"

docs.title: 3.5.1.13 Delete Face
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-face <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <id,id,...> is a comma-separated face-id list.
  • Every requested face id is deleted directly.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote delete-face "4,5"

docs.title: 3.5.1.14 Delete Rebar
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-rebar <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <id,id,...> is a comma-separated rebar-id list.
  • Every requested rebar id is deleted directly.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote delete-rebar "2,9"

docs.title: 3.5.1.15 Select
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] select <point|curve|face|rebar> <id,id,...> [--mode <replace|add|remove|toggle>]

Arguments and behavior:

  • <point|curve|face|rebar> chooses one geometry entity type.
  • <id,id,...> is a comma-separated positive-id list.
  • --mode replace rebuilds the selection from the requested ids.
  • --mode add, remove, and toggle update the current selection state in place.
  • The command changes selection only; it does not create or delete geometry.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote select curve "3,7,9" --mode add

docs.title: 3.5.1.16 Delete Selection
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] delete-selection

Arguments and behavior:

  • The command deletes the currently selected removable entities in the active section.
  • Faces and rebars in the selection are deleted immediately.
  • Curves referenced by faces are kept and remain selected.
  • Points referenced by curves or rebars are kept and remain selected.
  • If nothing removable is selected, the command succeeds as a no-op.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote select face "4"
hf2DStudio --remote delete-selection

docs.title: 3.5.1.17 Merge Selected Points
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] merge-selected-points

Arguments and behavior:

  • The command takes no positional arguments.
  • It inspects the current selected-point set in the active section.
  • Selected points that already share the same coordinates are merged into one shared topology point per coordinate group.
  • The surviving point keeps its existing id. Removed duplicate ids are reported in the result JSON.
  • This command is an explicit topology operation. Use move-point --merge on when you want to connect by moving one point onto another location intentionally.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote select point "12,18"
hf2DStudio --remote merge-selected-points

docs.title: 3.5.1.18 Detach Selected Points
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] detach-selected-points

Arguments and behavior:

  • The command takes no positional arguments.
  • It inspects the current selected-point set in the active section.
  • Each selected point shared by multiple curves is split into independent coincident points so the attached curves no longer share one topology point.
  • New duplicate point ids are reported in the result JSON.
  • Points still referenced by existing faces or rebars are blocked and left unchanged.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote select point "21"
hf2DStudio --remote detach-selected-points

docs.title: 3.5.1.19 Set Seed
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] set-seed --curve-ids <id,id,...> --seed <integer>

Arguments and behavior:

  • --curve-ids <id,id,...> is a comma-separated curve-id list.
  • --seed <integer> assigns one explicit seed count to every requested curve.
  • The seed must be a positive integer.
  • Lines accept 1 or greater. Arcs, bezier curves, and splines clamp to their built-in minimum seed when needed.
  • The command requires editable geometry and fails when any requested curve id is missing.
  • This command only assigns manual seeds. It does not run the TFI interval correction used by auto-seed.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote set-seed --curve-ids "2" --seed 3

docs.title: 3.5.1.20 Auto Seed
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] auto-seed --curve-ids <id,id,...>

Arguments and behavior:

  • --curve-ids <id,id,...> is a comma-separated curve-id list.
  • Cannot be combined with --seed.
  • Recomputes rough seed counts from the smallest max-H value found across the requested curves.
  • After the rough pass, tries conservative TFI interval correction on hole-free single-outer-loop faces whose outer-loop curves are all included in this --curve-ids set.
  • Correction only increases seeds on deficient sides. The per-face budget is min(4, max(1, ceil(totalSideIntervals * 0.20))); if the required correction is larger or ambiguous, the rough seeds are kept.
  • If the face has Quad Mesh Corner Hints, the hint plan is used before automatic corner candidates.
  • The command requires editable geometry and fails when any requested curve id is missing.
  • Produces the same result as the Auto Seed button in the GUI.
  • The success response's intervalCorrections value is the number of stored seed increments applied by the correction pass.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote auto-seed --curve-ids "1,2,3,4"

docs.title: 3.5.1.21 Generate Circle
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] generate-circle <radius> <yp> <zp>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <radius> must be a positive finite number.
  • <yp>, <zp> give the section coordinates of the center.
  • Creates one closed circle composed of four rational quadratic bezier segments.
  • Each segment seed is initialized to the current default curve seed of the section model.
  • The command requires editable geometry.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote generate-circle 50 0 0

docs.title: 3.5.1.22 Generate Circular Points
docs.text:
Syntax:

hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] generate-circular-points <radius> <yp> <zp> <start-angle-deg> <count>

Arguments and behavior:

  • <radius> must be a positive finite number.
  • <yp>, <zp> give the section coordinates of the center.
  • <start-angle-deg> is the angle of the first point; positive angles rotate from the +y axis toward the +z axis.
  • <count> is a positive integer that specifies how many points to create.
  • Creates <count> evenly spaced points on the circle of radius <radius>.
  • Creates points only; no curves are created. Useful for assembling rebar groups.
  • The command requires editable geometry.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote generate-circular-points 60 0 0 0 8

docs.title: 3.6.1 Definition
docs.text:
• Use definition commands to build the section-analysis input data: functions, materials, sections, template-mesh sections, and analysis definitions.
  • GUI Apply actions in the Function, Material, Section, and Analysis editors append the same IPC commands to the default script history.

docs.title: 3.6.1.1 Function
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] function <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--unit-system <text>]
  • Creates or updates one section *Function, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name> definition.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Empty function content is rejected.
  • Optional --unit-system <text> maps to the local UnitSystem= token for function types that allow local UnitSystem.
  • --unit-system is not accepted for function types that disallow local UnitSystem, including ConcreteTime.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • The command updates the section model in place and marks the current section model as changed.
  • Successful Apply in the Function editor records the same command into Remote Control History.
  • Concrete DB envelope inputs use the same syntax as the shared *Function command, but the allowed standards depend on the function type. For example, MaekawaTEnv content can be KDS-2026-C30, ACI318-2025-C4000, EC2-2004-C30, or those forms with a trailing , ToDirectForm. ParabolaCEnv is section-analysis input, accepts only the KDS/EC2 family, and may include alpha before ToDirectForm. For HognestadCEnv, EC2CEnv, and MPPCEnv, put EciCurve before ToDirectForm when the original initial curve is required. Do not include a local UnitSystem=... keyword in DB function input.
  • ConcreteTime supports the shared User, ... named-group form and EC2/KDS/ACI standard datalines. Standard content such as EC2-2004-C30, KDS-2026-C30, or ACI209-1992-C4000 requires a prior section global UnitSystem. The User, ... form only references existing functions and does not require the global UnitSystem at input time.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote function General LINEAR --content "0,0\n1,1"
hf2DStudio --remote function General CYCLE --content-file D:\Work\cycle.txt
hf2DStudio --remote function ParabolaCEnv EC2C30SectionC --content "EC2-2004-C30, 1.0/1.5"
hf2DStudio --remote function HognestadCEnv ACI4000C --content "ACI318-2025-C4000"
hf2DStudio --remote function EC2CEnv C30C --content "EC2-2004-C30"
hf2DStudio --remote function MaekawaTEnv C30T --content "KDS-2026-C30"
hf2DStudio --remote function ConcreteTime timeEC2 --content "EC2-2004-C30, 70, 200, 3, N"

docs.title: 3.6.1.2 Material
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] material <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--neg-stop-strain <value>] [--pos-stop-strain <value>] [--signal <text> | --signal-file <file>]
  • Creates or updates one section *Material, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • Optional --neg-stop-strain and --pos-stop-strain override the section-material stop strains after the material body is applied.
  • Optional --signal or --signal-file attaches section signal definitions to the same material.
  • --signal and --signal-file are mutually exclusive.
  • Inside --content and --signal, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty material content is rejected.
  • The command updates the section model in place and marks the current section model as changed.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote material UGeneric C30 --content "Compression, C30C, Plastic\nTension, C30T, Secant" --neg-stop-strain -0.003 --pos-stop-strain 0.00015
hf2DStudio --remote material USteel REBAR --content-file D:\Work\rebar-material.txt --signal-file D:\Work\rebar-signal.txt

docs.title: 3.6.1.3 Section
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] section <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--taper <on|off>]
  • Creates or updates one *Section, Name=<name> definition.
  • <name> must not be empty.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Empty section content is rejected.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • --taper on|off sets the taper flag of the section; when omitted the current flag is preserved.
  • After switching --taper on, new geometry can be authored independently on the left and right sides.
  • The command updates the section model in place and marks the current section model as changed.
  • Successful Apply in the Section editor records the same command into Remote Control History.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote section Sec-1 --content "..." --taper off
hf2DStudio --remote section Sec-1 --content-file D:\Work\section-body.txt --taper on

docs.title: 3.6.1.4 Template Mesh
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] template-mesh <H|T|C|2C|L|2L|HR> <name> --material <name> --H <value> (--B1 <value> --tw <value> --tf1 <value> | --B <value> --t <value> --r <value>) [--B2 <value>] [--tf2 <value>] [--c <value>] [--r1 <value>] [--r2 <value>] [--r3 <value>] [--r4 <value>]
  • Creates or updates one mesh-only standard section from Section Wizard dimensions.
  • The command uses the same template-mesh builder as the Section Wizard button.
  • It does not create section geometry; any existing geometry with the same section name is removed.
  • <H|T|C|2C|L|2L|HR>, <name>, --material, and --H are required.
  • For H/T/C/2C/L/2L, --B1, --tw, and --tf1 are required. --B2 defaults to --B1, --tf2 defaults to --tf1, and omitted --c/--r1/--r2/--r3/--r4 default to 0.
  • For HR, --B, --t, and --r are required. --B is the outer width, --t is wall thickness, and --r is the inner corner radius.
  • For 2C and 2L, --c 0 keeps the two section components topologically separate even where coordinates coincide.
  • The resulting mesh uses Q8 rectangular cells, T6 quarter-fillet cells, and HR annular-corner Q8 cells where applicable.
  • Section constants are computed immediately after the mesh is created.
  • The result JSON returns the section name, shape, material, whether an existing section was updated, and whether section constants were computed.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote template-mesh H H600 --material Steel --H 600 --B1 300 --tw 12 --tf1 20 --B2 300 --tf2 20 --r1 15 --r2 15
hf2DStudio --remote template-mesh 2L DL100 --material Steel --H 100 --B1 75 --tw 10 --tf1 10 --c 0 --r1 8 --r2 0 --r3 0
hf2DStudio --remote template-mesh HR HR300 --material Steel --H 300 --B 200 --t 12 --r 12

docs.title: 3.6.1.5 Analysis
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] analysis <name> --section <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--right <on|off>] [--ref <a,b,c>] [--output <Preselect|All>]
  • Creates or updates one *Analysis, Name=<name> definition.
  • <name> and --section <name> are both required and must not be empty.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Empty analysis content is rejected.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • --right on|off selects whether to use the right-side geometry of a taper section as the analysis target; default is off.
  • --ref <angle,yp,zp> supplies the rotation angle (deg) and origin of the analysis reference frame as a 3-field comma list; when omitted the section default reference is used.
  • --output <Preselect|All> chooses the result scope; default is Preselect.
  • The command updates the section model in place and marks the current section model as changed.
  • Successful Apply in the Analysis editor records the same command into Remote Control History.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote analysis Ana-1 --section Sec-1 --content-file D:\Work\analysis.txt
hf2DStudio --remote analysis Ana-R --section Sec-1 --content-file D:\Work\analysis.txt --right on --ref "0,0,0" --output All

docs.title: 3.6.1.6 Environment UnitSystem
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-unit-system get
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-unit-system set <force-length-time-temp|none>
  • Definition command notes:
  • exactly one of --content or --content-file is required where applicable
  • analysis requires --section
  • successful GUI edits in the Definition editors, including the Command panel Environment editor, are recorded with these same command forms
  • environment-unit-system get returns the current *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem token as JSON
  • environment-unit-system set accepts a force-length-time-temp 4-field token such as N-m-s-K, kN-cm-s-K, or N-mm-s-Celsius
  • environment-unit-system set none clears the section unit system
  • The command matches the Apply action of the Command panel Environment editor, and Remote Control History records it with the same form.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote environment-unit-system get
hf2DStudio --remote environment-unit-system set kN-cm-s-K
hf2DStudio --remote environment-unit-system set none

docs.title: 3.7 hf2DStudio Remote Control Operation and Analysis
3.7.1 Operation
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] make-mesh [build|delete|toggle]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] make-mesh --mode <build|delete|toggle>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] compute-section-constants [compute|invalidate|toggle]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] compute-section-constants --mode <compute|invalidate|toggle>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] renumber
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] move <top-left|top-middle|top-right|middle-left|middle-middle|middle-right|bottom-left|bottom-middle|bottom-right|centroid|shear-center|offset> [--offset <yp,zp>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] rotate <angle-deg>
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] export-section [--name <name>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] export-guide-geometry [--side <left|right>] [--ref-cs <name>] [--name <name>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] export-curve-mesh [--side <left|right>] [--node-id-offset <id>] [--element-id-offset <id>] [--ref-cs <name>]
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] export-domain-mesh [--side <left|right>] [--node-id-offset <id>] [--element-id-offset <id>] [--ref-cs <name>]
  • move offset requires --offset <yp,zp>.
  • make-mesh build builds the mesh and computes section constants together.
  • All export commands copy the exported text to the clipboard and also return the same text in the result JSON payload.
  • If the section model has a global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem, every export writes that UnitSystem block at the beginning of the exported text.

docs.title: 3.7.1.1 export-section
docs.text:
• Exports the active section definition as *Section, TYPE=Beam input text.
  • Options: --name <name> overrides the exported section name. When omitted, the current section name is used.
  • Validation: Requires an active section in the target hf2DStudio. Requires an existing section mesh.
  • Behavior: Copies the exported beam-section text to the clipboard. Returns the same text in the remote result JSON. The output includes the section definition and the section data needed to recreate the section input block. If the current section mesh contains quadratic cells, the exported *Cell, TYPE=Mesh block keeps the original T6/Q8 connectivity instead of silently downgrading it to T3/Q4.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote export-section

docs.title: 3.7.1.2 export-guide-geometry
docs.text:
• Exports the active section geometry as *Construction, TYPE=Guide text.
  • Options: --side <left|right> selects the side-dependent geometry to export when the section uses taper-aware data. --ref-cs <name> appends Ref=<name> to the exported *Construction keyword line. --name <name> overrides the exported construction name. When omitted, the current section name is used.
  • Validation: Requires an active section in the target hf2DStudio. Requires active geometry with curve data.
  • Behavior: Copies the generated guide geometry text to the clipboard. Returns the same text in the remote result JSON. Guide points are exported on the Z=0 plane using section yp/zp as x/y. The optional reference coordinate system name is written only on the exported keyword line. The output uses the Guide primitive form that matches the current section geometry.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote export-guide-geometry --side left --ref-cs CS-1 --name Guide-1

docs.title: 3.7.1.3 export-curve-mesh
docs.text:
• Exports the active section curves as a 1D curve mesh.
  • Options: --side <left|right> selects the side-dependent curve set when the geometry is side-aware. --node-id-offset <id> shifts generated node IDs by the specified offset. --element-id-offset <id> shifts generated element IDs by the specified offset. --ref-cs <name> assigns the reference coordinate system name used in the exported node block.
  • Validation: Requires an active section in the target hf2DStudio. Requires active geometry with curve data.
  • Behavior: Copies the exported curve mesh text to the clipboard. Returns the same text in the remote result JSON. The output follows the current curve-mesh export format used by the GUI. This is a seed-point-based 1D curve-mesh export. It uses the geometry curve sampling and writes the current 1D FE format used by the GUI, independent of the domain-mesh order.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote export-curve-mesh --side right --node-id-offset 1000 --element-id-offset 2000 --ref-cs CS-1

docs.title: 3.7.1.4 export-domain-mesh
docs.text:
• Exports the active section domain mesh as 2D FE input text.
  • Options: --side <left|right> selects the side-dependent domain when the section uses taper-aware data. --node-id-offset <id> shifts generated node IDs by the specified offset. --element-id-offset <id> shifts generated element IDs by the specified offset. --ref-cs <name> assigns the reference coordinate system name used in the exported text.
  • Validation: Requires an active section in the target hf2DStudio. Requires an existing section mesh.
  • Behavior: Copies the exported domain mesh text to the clipboard. Returns the same text in the remote result JSON. The export always follows the mesh-only domain-mesh format used by the GUI. The command preserves the current domain-mesh order. Linear meshes export CPS3/CPS4, and quadratic meshes export CPS6/CPS8.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote export-domain-mesh --side left --node-id-offset 1000 --element-id-offset 2000 --ref-cs CS-1

docs.title: 3.7.1.5 make-mesh
docs.text:
• Builds, deletes, or toggles the active section mesh.
  • Validation: build requires section geometry. delete removes the current mesh only when one exists.
  • Behavior: build creates the mesh and then computes section constants immediately. In other words, centroid, shear-center, and other derived section constants are prepared in the same step. The remote command does not take a linear/quadratic option. It uses the mesh-order state already held by the current hf2DStudio session. build uses the currently stored curve seeds and Quad Mesh Corner Hints; it does not rerun auto-seed interval correction or mutate seeds. If the TFI interval condition is not met, or if the candidate is not uniquely safe, that face continues through the Netgen fallback path. If a mesh already exists, build returns success without replacing it. Delete the current mesh first if you want to rebuild with a different order. In the GUI, the equivalent operations are Operation > Make Linear Mesh, Operation > Make Quadratic Mesh, and Operation > Delete Mesh.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote make-mesh build

docs.title: 3.7.1.6 compute-section-constants
docs.text:
• Computes, invalidates, or toggles section constants for the active section mesh.
  • Validation: Requires an existing mesh.
  • Behavior: Use this command when you want to recompute or invalidate section constants for an existing mesh. make-mesh build already computes section constants by default.

docs.title: 3.7.1.7 renumber
docs.text:
• Renumbers all geometry entities of the active section.
  • Syntax: renumber
  • Validation: No positional arguments. An active section must exist in the target hf2DStudio.
  • Behavior: Points, curves, faces, and rebars each get fresh ids starting from 1. All externally cached ids become invalid; the next step must query ids again. Produces the same result as GUI Operation > Renumber and is recorded into Remote Control History with the same command form.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote renumber

docs.title: 3.7.1.8 move
docs.text:
• Translates the whole active section by an anchor rule or an explicit offset.
  • Syntax: move <anchor> [--offset <yp,zp>]
  • Validation: <anchor> must be one of: top-left, top-middle, top-right, middle-left, middle-middle, middle-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right, centroid, shear-center, offset. --offset <yp,zp> is allowed only with the offset anchor, in which case it is required. Supplying --offset with any other anchor fails.
  • Behavior: The nine directional anchors move the axis-aligned bounding box so that the chosen anchor sits at the origin (0,0). centroid moves the current section-constants centroid to the origin; shear-center moves the shear center. offset translates the whole geometry by <yp,zp> without changing the anchor point itself. Matches the GUI Operation > Move actions and is recorded into Remote Control History with the same command form.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote move centroid
hf2DStudio --remote move offset --offset "10,5"

docs.title: 3.7.1.9 rotate
docs.text:
• Rotates the whole active section by the given angle.
  • Syntax: rotate <angle-deg>
  • Validation: The angle must be a single finite number. An active section must exist in the target hf2DStudio.
  • Behavior: Rotates the geometry about the current origin (yp=0, zp=0); positive angles rotate from the +y axis toward the +z axis. After rotating you can follow up with move centroid or move shear-center to realign the anchor if needed. Matches the GUI Operation > Rotate action and is recorded into Remote Control History with the same command form.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote rotate 30
hf2DStudio --remote rotate -90

docs.title: 3.7.2 Analysis
docs.text:
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] run-analysis
hf2DStudio --remote [--target <id>] unlock-model
  • Requires an existing saved file path.
  • If unsaved changes exist, auto-save is attempted before analysis starts.
  • No extra CLI options are accepted. The remote command uses the same analyzer launch path as the GUI action.
  • unlock-model mirrors the GUI Unlock model action and deletes the current section-analysis result so editing returns to preprocessing mode.
  • unlock-model is available only when a result file exists or analysis results are currently loaded.

docs.title: 3.7.2.1 run-analysis
docs.text:
• Starts section analysis in the same way as the GUI analysis action.
  • Validation: Requires a saved current file path. Fails if analysis is already running.
  • Behavior: If unsaved changes exist, the current file is saved first. Existing .xlsx result output for the current section file is removed before the new run starts.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote run-analysis

docs.title: 3.7.2.2 unlock-model
docs.text:
• Deletes the current section-analysis result and returns the model to editable preprocessing mode.
  • Validation: Takes no positional arguments. Fails while analysis is running. Fails when no saved or loaded result exists.
  • Behavior: Removes the current .xlsx analysis-result file when present. Clears loaded analysis result data from the active session even if only in-memory results remain. GUI Unlock model also appends the same canonical unlock-model tail to Remote Control History after success.

Example:

hf2DStudio --remote unlock-model

docs.title: 2.1.1 hfStudio Commands
docs.text:
Recommended starting order: list, status, open, save, window-state commands (focus, maximize, minimize) → selection → preprocessing.

Shared rules (target, scripts, session files, exit codes) are in Remote Control Basics. If the GUI is new, start with GUI Guide.

docs.title: 2.1.2 Command Groups
docs.text:
• Remote-only helpers: list, target, status, ping, focus, maximize, minimize, script, script-save
  • View: view
  • Window and file: open, save, import, export, write-scene, write-program-shot, quit
  • Display and selection: select, visibility, representation, transparency, element-shrink, section-view, parallel-projection, shading-color, display-control, grid-spacing, tool, camera, view
  • Preprocessing definitions and model history: undo, redo, coordinatesystem, coordinatesystem-activate, coordinatesystem-rename, coordinatesystem-delete, construction, construction-rename, construction-delete, function, function-rename, function-delete, material, material-rename, material-delete, load, load-rename, load-delete, sensor, sensor-rename, sensor-delete, section, section-rename, section-delete, assign-section, assign-beam-cs, assign-beam-end-release, assign-embedded-line-spline, assign-embedded-line-host-elset, assign-mck-element-scale-factor, assign-mck-element-cs, assign-moving-spring-initial-position, step, step-rename, step-delete, history, history-rename, history-delete, nset, nset-rename, nset-delete, elset, elset-rename, elset-delete, surface, merge-node-tolerance, coincidence-tolerance
  • Analysis and postprocessing: check-model, run-analysis, unlock-model, step-delete-from, post-*

docs.title: 2.1.3 Modeling Notes
docs.text:
• Definition commands use the same canonical tail format stored by script-save.
  • The assign-* family mirrors the preprocessing context-menu assign actions. It defaults to the current element selection, accepts --source <ids|__selected__>, and uses none only for clear-capable assignment commands.
  • Internally the assign-* commands build *Distribution, TYPE=... blocks. Clear flows use *Distribution, TYPE=..., Remove, so there is no separate distribution remote command anymore.
  • The coordinatesystem, construction, function, material, load, sensor, section, step, history, nset, and elset families cover create/update, rename, and delete flows that match the corresponding ModelTree actions. coordinatesystem-activate also mirrors the TreeMenu checked/unchecked path for User coordinate systems in a render view: use a name to activate it, or none to clear the active one.
  • Most definition commands still stay locked in postprocessing mode, but a small set of GUI-matched exception paths can still modify the current HDB there: environment-info set, nset, elset, step Post ..., step-delete-from ..., and history PostHistory ....
  • Rename and delete commands for step, history, nset, and elset remain preprocessing-only so remote execution stays non-interactive and avoids postprocessing confirmation flows.
  • undo and redo replay the current preprocessing model-history stack, so they depend on the active session state rather than declarative definition text.
  • All definition commands that edit block text accept either --content <text> or --content-file <file>.

docs.title: 2.1.4 Result Output
docs.text:
• Successful commands do not all print the same amount of result JSON.
  • Commands that always print result JSON include list, target, status, undo, redo, environment-*, merge-node-tolerance, coincidence-tolerance, grid-spacing, camera, and view.
  • Query-style postprocessing commands such as post-step get, post-frame get, post-scalar get, post-vector get, post-contour ... get, and post-scale ... get also print result JSON.
  • Most file actions, create/update/delete commands, and simple toggle commands return success or failure without extra JSON output.
  • Internal fields such as scriptTail are used for Remote Control History and script-save, and are hidden from normal result JSON output.

docs.title: 2.2 hfStudio Remote Control Remote-only
docs.text: Use these commands to discover target instances, inspect runtime state, and work with remote script files before sending model or view commands.

docs.title: 2.2.1 list
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote list
  • Prints the running hfStudio instances that can accept remote-control requests.
  • Use this first when you need an explicit target id for --target <id>.

docs.title: 2.2.2 target
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote target <set|show|clear> [id]
  • Manages the local default target used when --target is omitted.
  • set [id] stores the selected instance as the local default target.
  • show prints the current local default target.
  • clear removes the stored local default target.
  • target set/show/clear are local client commands and do not send remote-control requests to the GUI process.
  • See Remote Control Basics for the full target-selection flow.

docs.title: 2.2.3 status
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] status
  • Returns runtime status for the target instance.
  • Use it to confirm the current mode and runtime state before sending other commands.

docs.title: 2.2.4 ping
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] ping
  • Tests remote-control connectivity without changing model or view state.

docs.title: 2.2.5 focus
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] focus
  • Restores the window if needed, then raises and activates it.
  • This is a remote-only UI helper.
  • It does not change model data and does not append a canonical command tail to Remote Control History.

docs.title: 2.2.6 maximize
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] maximize
  • Switches the target window to the maximized state, then raises and activates it.
  • This is a remote-only UI helper.
  • It does not change model data and does not append a canonical command tail to Remote Control History.

docs.title: 2.2.7 minimize
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] minimize
  • Minimizes the target window.
  • This is a remote-only UI helper.
  • It does not change model data and does not append a canonical command tail to Remote Control History.

docs.title: 2.2.8 script
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--timeout-ms <ms>] script <file>
  • Runs a saved remote-control script file against the target instance.
  • --timeout-ms <ms> overrides the wait timeout for the whole script request.
  • The script file is interpreted as a sequence of remote-control command lines.

docs.title: 2.2.9 script-save
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] script-save [file]
  • Writes the accumulated Remote Control History tails to a file.
  • Without [file], the default script output path is used.
  • Use this when you want a replayable command script from the current session history.

Example:

hfStudio --remote list
hfStudio --remote target show
hfStudio --remote status
hfStudio --remote ping
hfStudio --remote maximize
hfStudio --remote focus
hfStudio --remote minimize
hfStudio --remote script-save D:\Work\hfStudio.ipc.txt
hfStudio --remote script D:\Work\hfStudio.ipc.txt

docs.title: 2.3 hfStudio Remote Control View
docs.text: Use this page for central-view control. Window-state helpers such as focus, maximize, and minimize are documented under Remote-only because they are UI-only remote helpers.

docs.title: 2.3.1 view
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] view list
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] view add <render|node-table|element-table|chart> [--placement <tab|split-h|split-v>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] view activate (--id <view-id> | current)
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] view close [--id <view-id> | current]
  • Manages only central widget views. It does not create or remove dock widgets such as ModelTree or command panels.
  • Scope:
  • central widget only
  • supported add types: render, node-table, element-table, chart
  • available in both preprocessing and postprocessing modes
  • View concepts:
  • currentView means the currently focused central view
  • activeRenderView means the render view used by display, camera, and rendering commands
  • currentView and activeRenderView can be different when the current central view is not a render view
  • view list:
  • returns JSON with count, currentViewId, activeRenderViewId, and views[]
  • each views[] item includes viewId, type, current, and tabIndex
  • render views also include activeRender
  • viewId uses a type prefix plus a per-type number such as r0, n0, e0, or c0
  • view add:
  • --placement tab adds a new tab
  • --placement split-h or split-v splits relative to the current view
  • view activate requires exactly one selector: current or --id
  • view close:
  • without a selector, closes the current view
  • --id targets a specific central view
  • closing the last remaining render view is rejected
  • when possible, previous current and active render views are preserved or restored

Example:

hfStudio --remote list
hfStudio --remote view list
hfStudio --remote view add chart --placement split-v
hfStudio --remote view activate --id c0

docs.title: 2.4 hfStudio Remote Control File
docs.text:
Use these commands to create, open, save, export, or close a model without using the GUI menus.

Most file commands stay silent on success. Internal history fields such as scriptTail are still recorded into Remote Control History and script-save, but are hidden from normal CLI JSON output.

docs.title: 2.4.1 new
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] new [--discard-unsaved]
  • Creates a new empty model.
  • Without --discard-unsaved, the command follows the same save-confirmation flow as GUI File > New.
  • If you choose Yes, the current model is saved first. If it has never been saved, the Save As dialog opens.
  • If you choose No, unsaved changes are discarded and a new empty model is created.
  • If you choose Cancel, the current model stays open and the command fails with NEW_FAILED.
  • --discard-unsaved discards unsaved changes immediately and does not show the GUI save-confirmation dialog.

docs.title: 2.4.2 open
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] open <file>
  • Opens the specified model file.
  • If unsaved changes exist and the current file already has a path, remote control auto-saves first.
  • If unsaved changes exist and there is no current file path, the command fails with SAVE_PATH_REQUIRED, except for an Untitled model whose only content is a global UnitSystem.

docs.title: 2.4.3 save
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] save [file]
  • Without [file], saves to the current file.
  • With [file], saves there and updates the current file path.

docs.title: 2.4.4 write-scene
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] write-scene <file>
  • Writes the active render scene to an output file.
  • Supported extensions:
  • .png
  • .jpg
  • .bmp
  • .pnm
  • .tif
  • .svg
  • .ps
  • .eps
  • .pdf
  • .tex

docs.title: 2.4.5 write-program-shot
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] write-program-shot <file>
  • Captures the full hfStudio program area, including menu bar, toolbars, dock widgets, central views, and status bar.
  • The parent directory of <file> must already exist.
  • The file extension must be supported by the current Qt image writer runtime.
  • Writes raster formats supported by the runtime.
  • Does not support vector formats such as .svg, .pdf, .ps, .eps, or .tex.
  • Records the canonical write-program-shot ... tail into Remote Control History and script-save.

docs.title: 2.4.6 import
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] import <file> [--type <Hyfeast|DXF|MGT|MCT|Abaqus|GMSH>]
  • Imports an external model file into the current session.
  • --type is optional.
  • DXF imports Guide primitives through the same DXF importer used by GUI File > Import.
  • DXF unit scaling is applied only when both the current DB/global UnitSystem and DXF $INSUNITS are valid; otherwise coordinates are imported without scaling.
  • The documented guaranteed scope is ASCII DXF with line/polyline-based entities such as LINE, LWPOLYLINE, and POLYLINE.
  • Binary DXF and version-specific advanced entities are outside the guaranteed support range.
  • When --type is omitted, the type is inferred from the extension:
  • .inp -> Hyfeast
  • .dxf -> DXF
  • .mgt -> MGT
  • .mct -> MCT
  • .msh -> GMSH

docs.title: 2.4.7 export
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] export <file>
  • Exports the current model to the specified output path.
  • Use an output path and extension supported by the existing export flow.

docs.title: 2.4.8 quit
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] quit [--discard-unsaved]
  • Closes the target window.
  • If unsaved changes exist and the current file already has a path, remote control auto-saves first.
  • If unsaved changes exist and there is no current file path, the command fails with SAVE_PATH_REQUIRED.
  • --discard-unsaved discards unsaved changes without auto-save, does not show the GUI save-confirmation dialog, and closes the target window immediately after the remote request is accepted.

Example:

hfStudio --remote open D:\Work\beam.inp
hfStudio --remote save
hfStudio --remote write-program-shot D:\Work\hfStudio-program.png
hfStudio --remote quit --discard-unsaved

docs.title: 2.5 hfStudio Remote Control Display
docs.text:
Use display commands when you want to change how the current model is shown without changing the model data itself.

By default these commands target activeRenderView. Use --view-id <rN> when you want to operate on a different render view without changing currentView or activeRenderView.

docs.title: 2.5.1 representation
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] representation <surface|wireframe|both>
  • Sets the main render representation mode.
  • Available values are surface, wireframe, and both.

docs.title: 2.5.2 transparency
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] transparency <on|off>
  • Turns transparent rendering on or off for the target render view.

docs.title: 2.5.3 element-shrink
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] element-shrink <on|off>
  • Turns element shrink display on or off for the target render view.

docs.title: 2.5.4 section-view
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] section-view <on|off>
  • Turns section-view clipping on or off for the target render view.

docs.title: 2.5.5 parallel-projection
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] parallel-projection <on|off>
  • Switches the target render view between perspective and parallel projection.

docs.title: 2.5.6 shading-color
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] shading-color <none|element-type|section>
  • Selects the shading-color source for the target render view.
  • Available values are none, element-type, and section.

docs.title: 2.5.7 display-control
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] display-control <item> <on|off>
  • Controls display toggles in the target render view.
  • <item> values:
  • origin-axes
  • corner-axes
  • grid
  • dimension-box
  • node
  • node-label
  • element-label
  • ecs
  • sensor-label
  • These items work in both preprocessing and postprocessing modes.

docs.title: 2.5.8 grid-spacing
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] grid-spacing get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] grid-spacing set <value>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] grid-spacing set auto
  • get returns the current grid spacing of the target render view as JSON.
  • set changes only the spacing value. It does not turn grid display on or off.
  • set <value> requires a positive finite number.
  • set auto matches the toolbar Auto Grid Spacing action and adjusts the spacing automatically for the current work-plane view.
  • set auto does not turn grid display on or off. It only adjusts the spacing value.
  • set auto is available whenever grid is on, except when the work-plane grid is hidden by an oblique view angle. If grid is off or hidden for an oblique view angle, the command returns INVALID_STATE.
  • When set auto succeeds, Remote Control History and script-save keep the semantic tail as grid-spacing set auto instead of expanding it to a resolved numeric value.

docs.title: 2.5.9 tool
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] tool distance [<p1> <p2>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] tool angle [<p1> <center> <p2>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] tool clear
  • Controls the render-view measurement tools shown under Display > Tool.
  • distance without point coordinates starts an interactive Distance Tool in the target render view.
  • angle without point coordinates starts an interactive Angle Tool in the target render view.
  • distance <p1> <p2> creates a completed Distance Tool directly.
  • angle <p1> <center> <p2> creates a completed Angle Tool directly.
  • Each point uses world-coordinate x,y,z numeric format.
  • clear clears existing Distance Tool and Angle Tool widgets in the target render view.
  • distance and angle return INVALID_STATE when another tool is still being placed or the target view is deformed.
  • clear returns INVALID_STATE when the target render view has no tools to clear. This matches the GUI Clear Tools action being enabled only while tools exist.
  • GUI Remote Control History records the coordinate form after the final point is placed, for example tool distance 0,0,0 100,0,0.

docs.title: 2.5.10 camera
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] camera get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] camera fit
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] camera view <iso-z|iso-y|iso-x|+x|-x|+y|-y|+z|-z>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] camera rotate <+x|-x|+y|-y|+z|-z>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] camera set --position <x,y,z> --focal-point <x,y,z> --view-up <x,y,z> [--projection <perspective|parallel>] [--view-angle <deg>] [--parallel-scale <value>] [--clipping-range <near,far>] [--roll <deg>] [--reset-clipping <on|off>]
  • Use camera get to read the current camera state as JSON.
  • Use camera fit, camera view, and camera rotate to change the active camera quickly.
  • camera set requires:
  • different position and focal-point
  • non-zero view-up

docs.title: 2.5.11 visibility
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] [--view-id <rN>] visibility <node|element|node-set|element-set|constraint|load|surface|construction|sensor> <items|all> <on|off>
  • Sets model-object visibility in the target render view.
  • Behavior matches ModelTree checkbox visibility, not global all-view visibility.
  • GUI ModelTree checkbox changes append the same canonical visibility ... tails to Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.
  • Target selectors:
  • node|element: use id,id,... or all
  • node-set|element-set: use name,name,...
  • constraint|load|surface|construction|sensor: use name,name,... or all
  • construction covers both splines and guides by name.

Example:

hfStudio --remote representation both
hfStudio --remote display-control origin-axes on
hfStudio --remote grid-spacing set 500
hfStudio --remote grid-spacing set auto
hfStudio --remote tool distance 0,0,0 100,0,0
hfStudio --remote tool angle 100,0,0 0,0,0 0,100,0
hfStudio --remote tool clear
hfStudio --remote camera fit
hfStudio --remote visibility construction "SplineA,Guide1" off

docs.title: 2.6 hfStudio Remote Control Selection
docs.text: Use selection commands to build the exact working set that later commands will act on.

docs.title: 2.6.1 select
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] select <node|element|constraint|load|spline|guide|surface|edge|sensor> <items|none> [--mode <current|union|intersection|xor|cur-diff-prev|prev-diff-cur>] [--ignore-missing]
  • Updates explicit selection for nodes, elements, named objects, surfaces, or edges.
  • node|element: use an integer id pattern such as 1,2,3, 1:3, 1:5:2, or none
  • constraint|load|spline|guide|sensor: use name,name,... or none
  • surface: use surfaceName, faceId@elementPattern, faceId@elsetName, or none
  • edge: use node-id chains such as 17-23 or 17-42-23, or none
  • --ignore-missing is available only for select node and select element
  • Without --ignore-missing, select node/element fails if any requested id is missing
  • With --ignore-missing, missing node/element ids are skipped and existing ids are selected
  • If --ignore-missing is used but every requested node/element id is missing, the command still fails with NOT_FOUND
  • Default mode is current
  • Remote Control History records the final current selection set, not the requested delta or mode expression
  • Remote Control History compacts node, element, and surface ids with the same integer-pattern format when possible

Example:

hfStudio --remote select node 1:100 --ignore-missing
hfStudio --remote select guide deckGuide --mode union
hfStudio --remote select edge "17-42-23,31-32" --mode union

docs.title: 2.7.1.1 environment-unit-system
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-unit-system get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-unit-system set <force-length-time-temp|none>
  • get returns the current global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem token as JSON.
  • set applies the same global UnitSystem behavior used by the GUI Environment > UnitSystem editor.
  • set requires preprocessing mode.
  • If set changes the length unit, hfStudio resets the camera to refit the resized model in the render views.
  • The value must be either:
  • a 4-field token such as kN-mm-s-K
  • none to clear the global UnitSystem
  • Clearing to none is rejected when local UnitSystem definitions still exist in functions or sections.
  • set returns INVALID_STATE when shared material functions would require incompatible unit conversion factors.
  • GUI Environment > UnitSystem Apply records the same canonical environment-unit-system set ... tail in Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.

Example:

hfStudio --remote environment-unit-system get
hfStudio --remote environment-unit-system set kN-mm-s-K
hfStudio --remote environment-unit-system set none

docs.title: 2.7.1.2 coincidence-tolerance
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] coincidence-tolerance get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] coincidence-tolerance set <non-negative-value>
  • Gets or sets the shared tolerance used by coincidence geometry checks.
  • The value is session-wide and is shared by:
  • node/element creation coincidence checks
  • divide/extrude intersection and zero-length validation
  • picking/intersection workflows that rely on coincidence tests
  • set requires a non-negative finite number.
  • get and set always print result JSON.
  • GUI Settings > General Apply records the same canonical coincidence-tolerance set ... tail in Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.

Example:

hfStudio --remote coincidence-tolerance get
hfStudio --remote coincidence-tolerance set 1e-10

docs.title: 2.7.1.3 environment-info
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-info get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] environment-info set (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • get returns the current normalized *Environment, TYPE=Info text as JSON.
  • set applies the same Info body content used by the GUI Environment > Info editor.
  • set is available in preprocessing mode and, as one of the few GUI-matched exceptions, also in postprocessing mode.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required for set.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.

docs.title: 2.7.12.1 function
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] function <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--unit-system <text>]
  • Creates or updates one *Function definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • function runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • Optional --unit-system <text> maps to the local UnitSystem= token on the *Function keyword line for function types that allow local UnitSystem.
  • --unit-system is not accepted for function types that disallow local UnitSystem, including ConcreteTime and ResponseSpectrum.
  • ConcreteTime standard content such as EC2-2004-C30, KDS-2026-C30, or ACI209-1992-C4000 requires a prior global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem. The User, ... named-group form only references existing functions and does not require the global UnitSystem at input time.
  • ResponseSpectrum content uses the same body lines as *Function, Type=ResponseSpectrum. A TimeSignal source uses TimeSignal, timeSignalName, seriesIndex, dampingRatio followed by the period-grid line. For KDS sources, the first content line is KDS17|KDS41, siteClass, effectiveGroundAcceleration[, dampingRatio]. KDS17 with S1 uses the rock-site expression, KDS17 with S2 to S5 uses the soil-site expression, and KDS41 uses the building design response acceleration spectrum expression. An optional period-grid line samples the KDS closed-form spectrum into direct MultiLinear data. The KDS dampingRatio token is accepted only for KDS17 with siteClass=S1.
  • The KDS effectiveGroundAcceleration value \(S\) has standard-specific meaning. For KDS17, it is the effective horizontal ground acceleration for the selected design ground-motion level; with the administrative-zone method, use \(S=Z\times I\). For KDS41, it is the effective ground acceleration of the 2400-year maximum considered earthquake, and the program applies the \(2/3\) design-level factor internally.
  • Content is passed directly to readFunctionModification(..., true) after the IPC layer prepends the computed *Function keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • Successful apply marks the database modified and refreshes the render pipeline.

Example:

hfStudio --remote function MultiLinear AMP1 --unit-system kN-mm-s-K --content "0, 0\n1, 1"
hfStudio --remote function ResponseSpectrum KDS41_S3 --content "KDS41, S3, 0.154"
hfStudio --remote function ConcreteTime timeEC2 --content "EC2-2004-C30, 70, 200, 3, N"

docs.title: 2.7.13.1 step
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] step <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--prev <name>] [--nlgeom <on|off>]
  • Creates or updates one step definition while preserving the original position of an existing step in the step list.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • step supports all listed step types in preprocessing mode.
  • In postprocessing mode, only <type>=Post is allowed. This is one of the few GUI-matched definition exceptions that remain editable there.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • Supported step types are:
  • Static
  • Static, Arclength
  • Static, Quasi
  • Dynamic
  • Seepage
  • Seepage, Transient
  • Frequency
  • ResponseSpectrum
  • ModelUpdating, Static
  • ModelUpdating, Modal
  • ModelUpdating, Bayesian
  • ShapeEstimation
  • Post
  • PerformanceEvaluation
  • Post creates *PostStep, Name=<name>. Other types create *Step, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name>.
  • Optional --prev <name> maps to Prev=<name> and is allowed for every type except Post and PerformanceEvaluation.
  • Optional --nlgeom <on|off> maps to NLGEOM=<ON|OFF> and is allowed only for Static, Static, Arclength, Static, Quasi, and Dynamic.
  • Content is passed directly to hfDBReader after the IPC layer prepends the computed *Step or *PostStep keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • In preprocessing mode, a successful apply marks the database modified and refreshes the render pipeline.
  • In postprocessing mode, a successful apply additionally runs runLastDataProcessingStep() and updates the DB file immediately, matching the GUI Step widget behavior.

Example:

hfStudio --remote step Static STEP1 --content "EquiTime, 0.1, 10\n*Activate, Type=Element\nALL"
hfStudio --remote step "Static, Arclength" STEP2 --prev STEP1 --nlgeom on --content-file D:\Work\step2.txt
hfStudio --remote step ResponseSpectrum RS-X --content-file D:\Work\rs-step.txt
hfStudio --remote step Post CHECK1 --content "elem-all\nSSF, D, sensor-check\n1.3*DC.2"

docs.title: 2.7.13.4 step-delete-from
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] step-delete-from <name>
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • name must be non-empty and must resolve to an existing result-step path that the TreeWidget Delete Steps From ... action can delete.
  • If name is an auxiliary result-step such as StepA.aux.modal, the delete range is resolved from its owner step (StepA).
  • The command uses the same delete path and guard rules as TreeWidget Delete Steps From ....
  • Successful execution modifies the current HDB result data immediately.
  • After success, hfStudio reloads result-step metadata from HDB right away so the current step/frame list stays in sync without reopening the file.
  • If no result steps remain after deletion, hfStudio switches back to preprocessing mode.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical step-delete-from ... tail.
