hfStudio --remote step-delete-from POST2

docs.title: 2.7.14.1 history
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] history <History|PostHistory> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *History or *PostHistory definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • <type> must be History or PostHistory.
  • <name> must not be empty.
  • Content is passed directly to readHistoryModification(..., true) after the IPC layer prepends the computed *History or *PostHistory keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • Existing history items are updated in place, preserving their current list position.
  • In preprocessing mode, a successful apply refreshes the render pipeline and marks the database modified.
  • In postprocessing mode, only <type>=PostHistory is allowed. This is one of the few GUI-matched definition exceptions that remain editable there.
  • In postprocessing mode, a successful apply additionally runs runLastPostHistory() and updates the DB file immediately, matching the GUI History widget behavior.
  • Reader rule reminder:
  • first data line is the target step list
  • second and later data lines are history requests
  • at least two data lines are required after the keyword line

Example:

hfStudio --remote history History H1 --content "STEP1, STEP2\nD.X@10, FK.X@10\nA.X@center_line"
hfStudio --remote history PostHistory HPOST --content-file D:\Work\post-history.txt

docs.title: 2.7.15.1 assign-*
docs.text: The assign-* commands mirror the preprocessing context-menu assign actions. They run only in preprocessing mode and target the current element selection by default.

docs.title: 2.7.15.1.1 Common Rules
docs.text:
• Use --source <ids|__selected__> to override the current element selection. The default is __selected__.
  • assign-section, assign-beam-cs, assign-beam-end-release, assign-embedded-line-spline, assign-embedded-line-host-elset, and assign-mck-element-cs accept none to clear the current assignment.
  • assign-mck-element-scale-factor and assign-moving-spring-initial-position always require explicit numeric values.
  • Internally these commands build one *Distribution, TYPE=... block. Clear flows use *Distribution, TYPE=..., Remove.

docs.title: 2.7.15.1.2 assign-section
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] assign-section <section|none> [--source <ids|__selected__>]
  • Assigns or clears TYPE=Section.

docs.title: 2.7.15.1.3 assign-beam-cs

hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] assign-beam-cs <beamcs|none> [--source <ids|__selected__>]

docs.title: 2.7.15.1.4 assign-beam-end-release

hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] assign-beam-end-release <code|none> [--source <ids|__selected__>]
  • Assigns or clears TYPE=BeamEndRelease.
  • <code> is a Rx1|Ry1|Rz1|Rx2|Ry2|Rz2 combination. For two-dimensional beams, only Rz1 and Rz2 are valid.

hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] assign-embedded-line-spline <spline|none> [--source <ids|__selected__>]

docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] assign-mck-element-scale-factor <value> [--source <ids|__selected__>]

hfStudio --remote assign-section girder --source 1:20

docs.title: 2.7.16.1 model
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] model <type> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Applies one *Model, TYPE=<type> block.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • model runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • <type> must not be empty.
  • Supported model types in the current reader path are:
  • Block2D
  • Block3D
  • Cylinder
  • Wall
  • RectangularTank
  • CylindericalTank
  • CurveExtrusion
  • FarField2D
  • FarField3D
  • FarField2Dx
  • FarField3Dx
  • Content is passed directly to readModel() after the IPC layer prepends the *Model keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • Successful apply preserves the existing per-view hidden node/element state for already hidden items, inserts newly created visible items into each view, refreshes topology, and resets the camera, matching the GUI Model widget behavior.

Example:

hfStudio --remote model Block2D --content "B1, auto, auto, CPS4, SEC1\n0,10,10\n0,5,5"
hfStudio --remote model FarField3D --content-file D:\Work\farfield3d-model.txt

docs.title: 2.7.17.1 renumber
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] renumber <selected-nodes|selected-elements|all-nodes|all-elements> <start-id> <+X|-X|+Y|-Y|+Z|-Z> <+X|-X|+Y|-Y|+Z|-Z> <+X|-X|+Y|-Y|+Z|-Z>
  • Applies the same operation as the GUI Renumbering widget.
  • renumber runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • <start-id> must be a positive integer.
  • The three priority tokens must each be one of +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z, and they must use three distinct axes.
  • Target rules:
  • selected-nodes: renumbers the current node selection only
  • selected-elements: renumbers the current element selection only
  • all-nodes: renumbers the full root nset
  • all-elements: renumbers the full root elset
  • Behavior rules:
  • selected-target modes require a non-empty current selection
  • when only selected nodes/elements are renumbered, overlapping ids in the unselected remainder are pushed out using the existing largest-number next-id rule, matching the GUI widget
  • after a successful apply, numbering-changed and database-modified states are raised and the model is re-rendered
  • GUI Renumbering Apply records the same canonical renumber ... tail in Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt

Example:

hfStudio --remote renumber selected-nodes 1001 +X -Y +Z
hfStudio --remote renumber all-elements 1 -Z +X +Y

docs.title: 2.7.18 hfStudio Remote Control Undo And Redo
2.7.18.1 undo
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] undo
  • Applies the same model-history operation as the GUI Undo action.
  • undo runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • It uses the current in-memory preprocessing model-history stack of the target session.
  • undo fails with NOTHING_TO_UNDO when no earlier snapshot is available.
  • Successful execution records the canonical undo tail into Remote Control History and script-save.
  • Successful result JSON includes canUndo and canRedo after the operation.
  • The GUI Undo action records the same canonical tail in Remote Control History.

docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] redo

  • redo runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • It uses the current in-memory preprocessing model-history stack of the target session.
  • redo fails with NOTHING_TO_REDO when no redo snapshot is available.
  • Successful execution records the canonical redo tail into Remote Control History and script-save.
  • Successful result JSON includes canUndo and canRedo after the operation.
  • The GUI Redo action records the same canonical tail in Remote Control History.

Example:

hfStudio --remote node 1 0,0,0
hfStudio --remote undo
hfStudio --remote redo

docs.title: 2.7.2.1 coordinatesystem
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *CoordinateSystem, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • coordinatesystem runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • Supported coordinate-system types are User, Orientation, and Beam.
  • <name> must be non-empty and uses the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The command builds the keyword header first and applies the remaining lines as the block body.
  • Names created here can be referenced later by commands such as element-update --beam-cs and element-update --orientation-cs.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical coordinatesystem ... --content ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem User girder_cs --content "1, 0, 0\n0, 0, 1\n0, 1, 0"

docs.title: 2.7.2.2 coordinatesystem-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Both names must be non-empty and use the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The source name must exist.
  • The target name must not collide with another coordinate system unless it normalizes to the same name, in which case the command succeeds as a no-op.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical coordinatesystem-rename ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-rename girder_cs girder_local

docs.title: 2.7.2.3 coordinatesystem-activate
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--view-id <rN>] coordinatesystem-activate <name|none>
  • Sets the named User coordinate system as the checked/active user coordinate system in the target render view.
  • Activating one User coordinate system automatically clears any previously active User coordinate system in that render view.
  • The command is available whenever the current model and target render view exist; it is not limited to preprocessing mode.
  • Only User coordinate systems are valid. Orientation and Beam coordinate systems return an error.
  • Use none to clear the active User coordinate system in the target render view.
  • --view-id <rN> targets a specific render view. Without it, the active render view is used.
  • The command follows the same render-view path as the TreeMenu check state and uncheck state, so it changes or clears the active UCS / 2D datum target for that render view only.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical coordinatesystem-activate ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-activate girder_local

hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-activate none

docs.title: 2.7.2.4 coordinatesystem-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-delete <name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • <name> must be non-empty and must resolve to an existing coordinate system.
  • The command uses the same delete path as ModelTree, so the same reference cleanup is applied to loads, constraints, beam assignments, and the active user coordinate system.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical coordinatesystem-delete ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote coordinatesystem-delete girder_local

docs.title: 2.7.3.1 construction
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote construction <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *Construction, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • construction runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • Supported construction types are Guide and Spline.
  • <name> must be non-empty and uses the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The command builds the keyword header first and applies the remaining lines as the block body.
  • When the result is a guide, hfStudio also updates the current guide selection to that object, matching the GUI widget behavior.
  • Names created here can be used directly by commands such as select spline, select guide, and visibility construction.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical construction ... --content ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote construction Guide deckGuide --content "Line, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0\nLine, 0, 5, 0, 10, 5, 0"
hfStudio --remote construction Guide arcGuide --content "Arc, 0, 0, 0, 5, 2, 0, 10, 0, 0"

docs.title: 2.7.3.2 construction-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote construction-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Both names must be non-empty and use the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The source name must exist.
  • The target name must not collide with another construction unless it normalizes to the same name, in which case the command succeeds as a no-op.
  • The render pipeline is refreshed so ModelTree visibility state stays aligned with the renamed construction object.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical construction-rename ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote construction-rename deckGuide gridGuide

docs.title: 2.7.3.3 construction-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote construction-delete <name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • <name> must be non-empty and must resolve to an existing construction object.
  • The command uses the same delete path as ModelTree delete.
  • Existing construction delete guards are preserved. For example, a spline still cannot be deleted while it is referenced by a line sensor.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical construction-delete ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote construction-delete gridGuide

docs.title: 2.7.4.1.1 node
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] node <id> <x,y,z> [--nset <name>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
  • Creates or updates one node in preprocessing mode.
  • <id> must be a positive integer.
  • <x,y,z> must be three finite numeric values.
  • If <id> does not exist, the command creates a new node.
  • If <id> already exists, the command updates that node coordinate.
  • --nset is optional and is supported only when creating a new node.
  • --merge-node is optional, defaults to off, and is supported only when creating a new node.
  • With --merge-node on, an existing coincident node within the current merge-node-tolerance is reused instead of creating a new node.
  • This is the canonical IPC/CLI form for Node Table create and coordinate-edit operations.

Example:

hfStudio --remote node 101 0,0,0
hfStudio --remote node 101 10,20,30
hfStudio --remote node 2001 10,20,30 --nset BASE
hfStudio --remote node 2001 10,20,30 --merge-node on

docs.title: 2.7.4.1.2 merge-node-tolerance
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] merge-node-tolerance get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] merge-node-tolerance set <non-negative-value>
  • Gets or sets the shared coincident-node tolerance used by Merge Node operations.
  • The value is session-wide and is shared by:
  • node --merge-node on
  • node-copy
  • element-extrude
  • element-divide
  • GUI widgets that expose Merge Node
  • set requires a non-negative finite number.
  • get and set always print result JSON.
  • Remote Control History and script-save keep the canonical tail merge-node-tolerance set ....

Example:

hfStudio --remote merge-node-tolerance get
hfStudio --remote merge-node-tolerance set 1e-6

docs.title: 2.7.4.1.3 node-copy
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] node-copy <translate-copy|translate-move|rotate-copy|rotate-move> [--source <text>] --direction-axis <text> [--distance-angle <text>] [--start-id <id>] [--nset <name>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
  • Applies the same operation as the GUI Copy Node widget.
  • --source uses nset-expression syntax:
  • integer ids or id patterns such as 1,2,3, 1:3, 1:9:2
  • existing nset names
  • __selected__ for the current UI node selection
  • -token to remove ids, nsets, or __selected__ from the source set
  • If --source is omitted, the default is __selected__.
  • --direction-axis uses the same numeric repeat syntax as the GUI:
  • translate: dx,dy,dz
  • rotate: x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2
  • --distance-angle uses the same repeat syntax as the GUI, such as 1,2,2@1.5 or 20,30,2@15.
  • translate-copy and rotate-copy require --start-id.
  • translate-move does not use --distance-angle.
  • --nset is optional and matches the GUI behavior by inserting source/result nodes into that nset.
  • --merge-node defaults to on.
  • With --merge-node on, coincident target nodes are reused using the current merge-node-tolerance.

Example:

hfStudio --remote node-copy translate-copy --source "__selected__" --direction-axis 1,0,0 --distance-angle 100,2@50 --start-id 1001 --nset COPIED --merge-node on
hfStudio --remote node-copy rotate-move --source "TOP_NODES,-__selected__" --direction-axis 0,0,0,0,0,1 --distance-angle 15

docs.title: 2.7.4.1.4 node-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] node-delete <ids|__selected__>
  • Deletes nodes by id pattern or current node selection in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same safe delete behavior as the GUI.
  • <ids> accepts integer id patterns such as 1,2,3, 1:5, 1:9:2.
  • __selected__ resolves to the current node selection.
  • This is the canonical IPC/CLI form for Node Table row deletion.
  • Validation rules:
  • preprocessing mode only
  • every requested id must already exist before deletion starts
  • __selected__ requires a non-empty current node selection
  • Partial delete behavior:
  • safe delete may leave some requested nodes undeleted
  • when that happens, the command returns DELETE_PARTIAL with requestedIds, deletedIds, remainingIds, counts, and the canonical scriptTail
  • the applied tail is still recorded in Remote Control History because the model has changed

Example:

hfStudio --remote node-delete 101:105
hfStudio --remote node-delete __selected__

docs.title: 2.7.4.2.1 nset
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] nset <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *Nset, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Available in both preprocessing and postprocessing modes.
  • This is one of the few definition commands that remain editable in postprocessing mode.
  • Behavior rules:
  • preprocessing: creates a new set or updates an existing set
  • postprocessing: creates a new set, or updates an existing set only when that nset is not used by other objects
  • in postprocessing, a successful apply updates the model in the current DB/HDB file immediately, matching the GUI Define NSet widget behavior
  • Content uses the same body syntax as the Define NSet GUI:
  • integer ids or id patterns such as 1,2,3, 1:3, 1:9:2
  • existing nset names
  • -token to remove nodes or referenced sets from the target set
  • __selected__ expands to the current node selection
  • -__selected__ removes the current node selection from the target set

Examples:

hfStudio --remote nset LEFT_EDGE --content "1:61:10\nTOP_LINE"
hfStudio --remote nset PICKED --content "__selected__,BASE_NODES,-101:120"
hfStudio --remote nset REVIEW_PICK --content "__selected__"

docs.title: 2.7.4.2.2 nset-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] nset-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Renames one node-set definition.
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same name normalization and duplicate-name checks as ModelTree rename.

Example:

hfStudio --remote nset-rename LEFT_EDGE LEFT_EDGE_REVIEW

docs.title: 2.7.4.2.3 nset-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] nset-delete <name>
  • Deletes one node-set definition.
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same dependency cleanup as ModelTree delete:
  • referenced loads and constraints drop the deleted nset reference
  • the command fails when the named nset cannot be deleted

Example:

hfStudio --remote nset-delete LEFT_EDGE_REVIEW

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.1 element
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element <type> <id> <n1,n2,...> [--section <name>] [--elset <name>]
  • Creates one element in preprocessing mode.
  • <id> must be a positive integer.
  • <n1,n2,...> must match the required node count for <type>.
  • All referenced node ids must already exist.

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.2 element-update
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-update <id> <n1,n2,...> [--section <name|none>] [--beam-cs <beamcs|none>] [--release <code|none>] [--scale-factor <value>] [--orientation-cs <ucs|none>] [--moving-position <x,y>] [--spline <spline|none>] [--host-elset <host-elset|none>]
  • Updates one existing element in preprocessing mode.
  • This is the canonical IPC/CLI form for Element Table row edits and non-row delete clears.
  • <id> must already exist.
  • <n1,n2,...> must match the current element node count.
  • Optional fields apply only to compatible element types:
  • --beam-cs: T3D2, B3D2H, B3D2MH
  • --release: B2D2H, B2D2MH, B3D2H, B3D2MH
  • --scale-factor, --orientation-cs: Spring, EarthSpring, PointMass
  • --moving-position: MovingSpring
  • --spline, --host-elset: EmbeddedLine
  • Use none to clear section / coordinate system / spline / host elset values.

Example:

hfStudio --remote element-update 201 11,12 --section BEAM_SEC --beam-cs CS_LOCAL --release none

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.3 element-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-delete <ids|__selected__>
  • Deletes elements by id pattern or current element selection in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same delete path as Element Table full-row deletion.
  • GUI Delete Node/Element Selection records explicit element-delete <ids> and node-delete <ids> tails in that order, using the selection snapshot captured at click time.
  • <ids> accepts integer id patterns such as 1,2,3, 1:5, 1:9:2.
  • __selected__ resolves to the current element selection.
  • Validation rules:
  • preprocessing mode only
  • every requested id must already exist before deletion starts
  • __selected__ requires a non-empty current element selection
  • Partial delete behavior:
  • safe delete may leave some requested elements undeleted
  • when that happens, the command returns DELETE_PARTIAL with requestedIds, deletedIds, remainingIds, counts, and the canonical scriptTail
  • the applied tail is still recorded in Remote Control History because the model has changed

Example:

hfStudio --remote element-delete 201:205
hfStudio --remote element-delete __selected__

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.4 element-extrude
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-extrude <translate|rotate> --direction-axis <text> --distance-angle <text> [--start-node-id <id>] [--start-element-id <id>] [--line2 <type>] [--quad4 <type>] [--prism6 <type>] [--hexa8 <type>] [--nset <name>] [--elset <name>] [--remove-source <on|off>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
  • Applies the same operation as the GUI Element Extrude widget.
  • The command uses the current eligible GUI selection and does not take a separate source argument.
  • Eligible sources are processed together, matching the GUI behavior:
  • selected nodes -> line elements
  • selected beam elements, selected Face2D edges, or selected edges -> quad elements
  • selected Solid2D/Shell elements or selected Face3D faces -> prism/hexa elements
  • --line2, --quad4, --prism6, and --hexa8 are optional result-type overrides. They are consumed only when the current selection produces that result category.
  • --direction-axis uses the same numeric repeat syntax as the GUI:
  • translate: dx,dy,dz
  • rotate: x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2
  • --distance-angle uses the same repeat syntax as the GUI, such as 100,2@50 or 15,30,3@10.
  • Default values are applied by result category when the corresponding result is produced and the option is omitted:
  • --start-node-id: current next node id
  • --start-element-id: current next element id
  • node -> line result: --line2 B3D2H
  • beam/edge -> quad result: --quad4 S4F
  • triangle face -> prism result: --prism6 C3D6
  • quad face -> hexa result: --hexa8 C3D8
  • --remove-source on
  • --merge-node on
  • Validation rules:
  • preprocessing mode only
  • translate requires exactly 3 direction values
  • rotate requires exactly 6 direction values and two distinct axis points
  • --distance-angle must resolve to one or more finite values
  • the current selection must contain at least one eligible source
  • Behavior rules:
  • --nset inserts source/result nodes into that nset, matching the GUI
  • --elset inserts created elements, and also selected source beam/shell/solid2d elements into that elset just like the GUI widget
  • --remove-source on removes source beam/shell/solid2d elements after extrusion; surface/edge sources are not deleted
  • --merge-node on merges coincident target nodes using the current shared merge-node-tolerance value
  • a node-only extrusion uses --line2 only; unused result-type options may be present but have no effect
  • Remote Control History records one canonical element-extrude ... tail, so exact replay assumes the same selection has already been reconstructed

Example:

hfStudio --remote select node 101,102
hfStudio --remote element-extrude translate --direction-axis 0,0,1 --distance-angle 100,2@50 --start-node-id 1001 --start-element-id 2001 --line2 T3D2 --quad4 S4F --prism6 C3D6 --hexa8 C3D8 --nset EXTRUDE_N --elset EXTRUDE_E --remove-source on --merge-node on

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.5 element-divide
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-divide refine --source <ids|__selected__> --segments <n> [--start-node-id <id>] [--start-element-id <id>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-divide topology --edge-source <text|__selected__> --segments <n> [--start-node-id <id>] [--start-element-id <id>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-divide parametric --source <ids|__selected__> --r <text> [--s <text>] [--t <text>] [--start-node-id <id>] [--start-element-id <id>] [--merge-node <on|off>]
  • Applies the same operation family as the GUI Element Divide widget.
  • refine and parametric use --source with element id patterns or __selected__.
  • topology uses --edge-source with comma-separated edge tokens like 11-12,12-13 or __selected__.
  • --segments must be a positive integer for refine and topology.
  • --r, --s, and --t use the same numeric repeat syntax as the GUI.
  • parametric requires --r
  • omitted --s or --t default to 1
  • Default values:
  • --start-node-id: current next node id
  • --start-element-id: current next element id
  • --merge-node on
  • Validation rules:
  • preprocessing mode only
  • every explicit source id must already exist
  • __selected__ requires a non-empty current element or edge selection
  • topology resolves each edge token against the current database edge topology
  • Behavior rules:
  • GUI refine and parametric history records explicit element id snapshots
  • GUI topology history records --edge-source __selected__, matching the current selected-edge command behavior
  • remote CLI/script may use __selected__, and that token is preserved in the canonical tail
  • --merge-node on merges coincident target nodes using the current shared merge-node-tolerance value
  • created elements become the new element selection, matching the GUI

Example:

hfStudio --remote element-divide refine --source 201:220 --segments 3 --start-node-id 1001 --start-element-id 2001 --merge-node on
hfStudio --remote element-divide topology --edge-source 11-12,12-13 --segments 2
hfStudio --remote element-divide parametric --source __selected__ --r 1,2,2@1.5 --s 1 --t 1

docs.title: 2.7.5.1.6 element-change
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-change retype --source <ids|__selected__> [--line2 <type>] [--tri3 <type>] [--quad4 <type>] [--tetra4 <type>] [--prism6 <type>] [--hexa8 <type>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-change reverse-node-order --source <ids|__selected__>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] element-change explode --source <ids|__selected__> --line2 <type> --tri3 <type> --quad4 <type> [--start-element-id <id>] [--remove-source <on|off>]
  • Applies the same operation family as the GUI Element Change widget.
  • --source accepts element id patterns or __selected__.
  • retype rules:
  • at least one family option is required
  • each supplied target type must match its family node count
  • GUI Remote Control History records all six family targets for deterministic replay
  • reverse-node-order uses only --source.
  • explode rules:
  • requires --line2, --tri3, and --quad4
  • default --start-element-id is the current LargestNumber next element id, matching the GUI widget
  • --remove-source defaults to on
  • Behavior rules:
  • retype returns the number of elements that actually changed
  • reverse-node-order affects only the same supported element families as the GUI
  • explode creates boundary elements, selects the created results, and optionally removes source elements
  • GUI Remote Control History records explicit source snapshots, not __selected__

Example:

hfStudio --remote element-change retype --source 201:260 --line2 B3D2H --tri3 S3F --quad4 S4F --tetra4 C3D4 --prism6 C3D6 --hexa8 C3D8
hfStudio --remote element-change reverse-node-order --source __selected__
hfStudio --remote element-change explode --source 401:420 --line2 B2D2H --tri3 CPS3 --quad4 CPS4 --start-element-id 9001 --remove-source on

docs.title: 2.7.5.2.1 elset
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] elset <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *Elset, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Available in both preprocessing and postprocessing modes.
  • This is one of the few definition commands that remain editable in postprocessing mode.
  • Behavior rules:
  • preprocessing: creates a new set or updates an existing set
  • postprocessing: creates a new set, or updates an existing set only when that elset is not used by other objects
  • in postprocessing, a successful apply updates the model in the current DB/HDB file immediately, matching the GUI Define Elset widget behavior
  • Content uses the same body syntax as the Define Elset GUI:
  • integer ids or id patterns such as 10,20,30, 100:110, 1:101:10
  • existing elset names
  • -token to remove elements or referenced sets from the target set
  • __selected__ expands to the current element selection
  • -__selected__ removes the current element selection from the target set

Examples:

hfStudio --remote elset COLUMN --content "101:120\nFRAME_OUTER"
hfStudio --remote elset PICKED --content "__selected__,FRAME_OUTER"
hfStudio --remote elset POST_FACE --content "__selected__,-FRAME_OUTER"

docs.title: 2.7.5.2.2 elset-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] elset-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Renames one element-set definition.
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same name normalization and duplicate-name checks as ModelTree rename.

Example:

hfStudio --remote elset-rename COLUMN COLUMN_REVIEW

docs.title: 2.7.5.2.3 elset-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] elset-delete <name>
  • Deletes one element-set definition.
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Uses the same dependency cleanup as ModelTree delete:
  • referenced loads, constraints, embedded-line host elsets, and step target lists are updated automatically
  • the command fails when the named elset cannot be deleted

Example:

hfStudio --remote elset-delete COLUMN_REVIEW

docs.title: 2.7.6.1 load
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] load <type> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>) [--func <name>]
  • Creates or updates one *Load, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name>[, Func=<name>] definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • load runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • --func <name> is optional and must refer to an existing function when used.
  • Supported load types are:
  • Concentric
  • Displacement
  • Gravity
  • SeismicRelative
  • Temperature
  • LineDistributed
  • SurfaceDistributed
  • LineMoving
  • SurfaceMoving
  • PedestrianMoving
  • FreeFieldSeismic
  • Content is passed directly to readLoadModification(..., true) after the IPC layer prepends the *Load keyword line.
  • For LineDistributed, content may include HydroStaticPressure lines in the same format as the command manual: line, HydroStaticPressure, gamma, gdx, gdy, gdz, fsx, fsy, fsz, width, +Y|-Y|+Z|-Z[, fnIdx]. The direction token is based on each beam element's ECS.
  • For SurfaceDistributed, content may include HydroStaticPressure lines in the same format as the command manual: surface, HydroStaticPressure, gamma, gdx, gdy, gdz, fsx, fsy, fsz[, +N|-N][, fnIdx]. -N is the default direction, and +N reverses the pressure to the surface normal direction. The remote command passes --content through the same load parser used by the GUI; no alias is accepted for HydroStaticPressure.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • After a successful apply, the created or updated load becomes the current load selection, matching the GUI Load widget behavior.
  • A newly created LineDistributed or SurfaceDistributed load is also registered as visible in the current render views so its distributed-load glyphs appear immediately.

Example:

hfStudio --remote load Gravity DEAD --content "ALL, 0, 0, -9.81"
hfStudio --remote load LineDistributed TUNNEL_WATER --content "lining, HydroStaticPressure, 9810, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 20, 1.0, -Y"
hfStudio --remote load SurfaceDistributed HYDRO --content "wall, HydroStaticPressure, 9810, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 20, +N"
hfStudio --remote load Concentric LIVE --func TIME1 --content-file D:\Work\concentric-load.txt

docs.title: 2.7.6.2 load-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] load-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Both names must be non-empty and use the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The source name must exist.
  • The target name must not collide with another load unless it normalizes to the same name, in which case the command succeeds as a no-op.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical load-rename ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote load-rename DEAD DEAD_G

docs.title: 2.7.6.3 load-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] load-delete <name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • name must be non-empty and must resolve to an existing load.
  • The command uses the same delete path as ModelTree delete, so step references and current load selection are cleaned up together.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical load-delete ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote load-delete DEAD_G

docs.title: 2.7.7.1 surface
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] surface <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *Surface, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • Content uses the same body syntax as the Define Surface GUI:
  • faceId@elementPattern
  • faceId@elsetName
  • existing surface names
  • __selected__ expands to the current face/surface selection
  • -__selected__ is not supported for surface.

Example:

hfStudio --remote surface TOP_FACE --content "__selected__"
hfStudio --remote surface SIDE_FACE --content "2@1:40,OTHER_SURFACE"

docs.title: 2.7.8.1 sensor
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] sensor <Point|Line|TrackTwist> <name> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Creates or updates one *Sensor, TYPE=<type>, Name=<name> definition.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • sensor runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • <type> and <name> must not be empty.
  • Supported sensor types are:
  • Point
  • Line
  • TrackTwist
  • Content is passed directly to readSensorModification() after the IPC layer prepends the *Sensor keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • After a successful apply, the created or updated sensor becomes the current sensor selection, matching the GUI Define Sensor widget.
  • Validation follows the existing sensor reader rules:
  • Point: first data line must be <field>, <hostElset>, later lines are id, x, y, z, dx, dy, dz
  • Line: first data line must be <field>, <hostElset>, <spline>[, <startId>]
  • TrackTwist: single data line must be <line1Elset>, <line2Elset>, <spacing>, <advance>[, <startId>]

Example:

hfStudio --remote sensor Point SG1 --content "Strain, girder\n1, 1, 0.0, 0, 1, 0, 0"
hfStudio --remote sensor Line LVDT1 --content-file D:\Work\line-sensor.txt
hfStudio --remote sensor TrackTwist TW1 --content "leftRail, rightRail, 3, 0.5, 1"

docs.title: 2.7.8.2 sensor-rename
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] sensor-rename <old-name> <new-name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • Both names must be non-empty and use the same single-token normalization as GUI edits.
  • The source name must exist.
  • The target name must not collide with another sensor unless it normalizes to the same name, in which case the command succeeds as a no-op.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical sensor-rename ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote sensor-rename SG1 SG_MAIN

docs.title: 2.7.8.3 sensor-delete
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] sensor-delete <name>
  • Available only in preprocessing mode.
  • name must be non-empty and must resolve to an existing sensor.
  • The command uses the same delete path as ModelTree delete, so related output requests and post targets are cleaned up together.
  • Successful execution is recorded by script-save as a canonical sensor-delete ... tail.

Example:

hfStudio --remote sensor-delete SG_MAIN

docs.title: 2.7.9.1 nprop
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] nprop <ShellThickness|ShellDirector> (--content <text> | --content-file <file>)
  • Replaces one *NProp, TYPE=<type> block, matching the GUI Define NProp widget semantics.
  • Exactly one of --content or --content-file is required.
  • nprop runs only in preprocessing mode.
  • Supported NProp types are:
  • ShellThickness
  • ShellDirector
  • Content is passed directly to readNPropReset() after the IPC layer prepends the *NProp keyword line.
  • Inside --content, use \n for line breaks. \\n stays literal.
  • Empty content is rejected.
  • Successful GUI Define NProp > Apply also appends the same canonical nprop ... tail to Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.
  • Applying NProp marks topology/selection-topology changed, matching the current widget behavior.

Example:

hfStudio --remote nprop ShellThickness --content "left, 0.1\n1:10:2, 0.2"
hfStudio --remote nprop ShellDirector --content-file D:\Work\shell-director.txt

docs.title: 2.8 hfStudio Remote Control Analysis
docs.text: Use these commands to validate the model, start analysis, or return a solved model back to editable preprocessing mode.

docs.title: 2.8.1 check-model
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] check-model
  • Follows the existing validation path and does not change render mode.
  • GUI Check Model appends the same canonical check-model tail to Remote Control History after successful validation.

docs.title: 2.8.2 run-analysis
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] run-analysis [--ncpu <n>]
  • In preprocessing mode, starts analysis in the same way as the GUI Run Analysis action.
  • --ncpu <n> applies to the preprocessing start-analysis path.
  • Requires a saved current file path only for the preprocessing start-analysis path.
  • If unsaved changes exist, remote control uses the same save-first flow before starting analysis.
  • GUI Run Analysis appends the same canonical run-analysis tail to Remote Control History after a successful action.

docs.title: 2.8.3 unlock-model
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] unlock-model
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • Mirrors the GUI Unlock model action.
  • Removes all result steps so the model returns to preprocessing mode.
  • GUI Unlock model appends the same canonical unlock-model tail to Remote Control History after a successful action.

Example:

hfStudio --remote check-model
hfStudio --remote run-analysis --ncpu 8
hfStudio --remote unlock-model

docs.title: 2.9 hfStudio Remote Control Postprocessing
docs.text:
Use these commands after analysis results are available and you want to switch steps, frames, contours, vectors, scales, or overlay displays.

get queries return JSON and do not append a scriptTail. Set-type commands append canonical post-* ... tails to Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.

Most definition commands remain preprocessing-only, but postprocessing mode still keeps a few GUI-matched exception paths that can modify the current HDB: environment-info set, nset, elset, step Post ..., step-delete-from ..., and history PostHistory ....

docs.title: 2.9.1 post-plot
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-plot <contour|diagram|vector|sensor|deformed> <on|off>
  • Controls postprocessing plot toggles in the active view.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • deformed on fails when the current result step does not contain displacement output D.

docs.title: 2.9.2 post-step
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-step <step-name>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-step get
  • post-step <step-name> selects the named result step and moves to frame 1 of that step.
  • post-step get returns the current step and frame state as JSON.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • <step-name> must match an existing result-step name exactly.
  • The single token get is reserved as a query keyword for this command.

docs.title: 2.9.3 post-frame
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-frame <frame-index>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-frame get
  • post-frame <frame-index> selects a frame in the current result step.
  • post-frame get returns the current step and frame state as JSON.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • <frame-index> is 1-based and must be within the current step frame count.

docs.title: 2.9.4 post-scalar
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scalar <field> [<average-threshold>]
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scalar get
  • Selects the scalar field for the active result step.
  • get returns the current scalar field state as JSON.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • <field> must be a valid scalar field name for the current step and frame.
  • [<average-threshold>] is optional and must be an integer between 0 and 100.
  • <average-threshold> controls whether extrapolated element scalar values are averaged at shared element nodes. 0 disables averaging, while 1..100 averages values in the same averaging group only when they satisfy:
\[ \max(v_i)-\min(v_i) \le \frac{\mathrm{threshold}}{100} \left(\max(v_\mathrm{region})-\min(v_\mathrm{region})\right) \]
  • Averaging groups are formed within the same section, and \(v_\mathrm{region}\) is the scalar value range of that section group. Continuum elements average by shared node. Shell elements keep bottom/top values separate and average only values with the same shell element coordinate system. Beam elements average only values with the same section/material point index and beam element coordinate system.

docs.title: 2.9.5 post-vector
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-vector <field>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-vector get
  • Selects the vector or tensor field for the active result step.
  • get returns the current vector field state as JSON.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • <field> must be a valid vector or tensor field name for the current step and frame.

docs.title: 2.9.6 post-contour
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour auto-range <on|off>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour auto-range get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour range <min> <max>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour range get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour bands <n>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour bands get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour mode <uniform|custom>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour mode get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour levels <v1,v2,...>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour levels get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour overlay <text>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour overlay get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour overlay-color <r,g,b[,a]>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-contour overlay-color get
  • Controls contour settings in the active postprocessing view.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • auto-range, range, and bands set operations are rejected while custom contour mode is active.
  • mode custom initializes custom boundary levels from the current uniform range and band state when needed.
  • levels set requires between 2 and 31 strictly increasing boundary values.
  • overlay-color uses integer 0..255 channel values.
  • get returns the full contour state as JSON, plus action-specific aliases such as enabled, min, max, text, or color.

docs.title: 2.9.7 post-scale
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale deformed auto <on|off>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale deformed auto get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale deformed value <scale>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale deformed value get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale diagram auto <on|off>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale diagram auto get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale diagram value <scale>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale diagram value get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale vector auto <on|off>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale vector auto get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale vector value <scale>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale vector value get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale sensor auto <on|off>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale sensor auto get
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale sensor <e|d|v|a> <scale>
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-scale sensor <e|d|v|a> get
  • Controls deformed, diagram, vector, and sensor scale factors in the active postprocessing view.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • Explicit value or e|d|v|a inputs disable the corresponding auto-scale mode first.
  • get returns the full scale state as JSON, plus query-specific aliases such as enabled or value.

docs.title: 2.9.8 post-display
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-display <information|scalarbar|min-max-tag> <on|off>
  • Toggles postprocessing overlay and display items in the active view.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • information: upper-left information text
  • scalarbar: scalar bar widget
  • min-max-tag: min and max caption tags

docs.title: 2.9.9 post-animation-time-history
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-animation-time-history <on|off>
  • Matches Postprocessing > Play > Time History Ani.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • Fails if scale-factor animation is currently active.

docs.title: 2.9.10 post-animation-scale-factor
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-animation-scale-factor <on|off>
  • Matches Postprocessing > Play > Scale Factor Ani.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • Fails if time-history animation is currently active.

docs.title: 2.9.11 post-animation-loop
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-animation-loop <on|off>
  • Matches Postprocessing > Play > Loop.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • Controls whether the current animation repeats automatically.

docs.title: 2.9.12 post-animation-record
docs.text:
hfStudio --remote [--target <id>] post-animation-record <on|off> [<file>]
  • Matches Postprocessing > Play > Record.
  • Available only in postprocessing mode.
  • on requires a writable output file path with .avi or .mp4 extension.
  • off clears the current animation record target.
  • Can be changed only while no animation is active.

Example:

hfStudio --remote post-step "LC1-DeadLoad"
hfStudio --remote post-frame 7
hfStudio --remote post-scalar "S.Mises" 85
hfStudio --remote post-contour mode get
hfStudio --remote post-animation-record on "D:/work/result.avi"

docs.title: 1 Overview
docs.text:
2D Modeling and Section Tools is a set of tools for calculating sectional constants and performing nonlinear sectional analysis on arbitrary-shaped beam cross-sections.

  • hf2DStudio: 2D modeling and sectional-analysis GUI workspace
  • hfSectAnalyzer: sectional-analysis CLI solver

Many users start in hf2DStudio to create the section and review results, then move to an hfSectAnalyzer-centered workflow when repeatability or solver-side control becomes more important.

docs.title: 1.1 When to use it
docs.text:
Use the section tools when the main question is about section properties or section behavior.

  • sectional constants
  • nonlinear section analysis
  • reinforced or prestressed section review
  • chart/contour-based section interpretation

Choose the GUI-first path when you need visual geometry editing; choose the command-first path when you need repeatable section-analysis inputs.

docs.title: 1.2 Recommended path for first-time users
docs.text:
If you are new to the section tools, the recommended order is:

  1. Use this page to understand the overall role of the section tools.
  2. If you are GUI-first, continue with hf2DStudio Help.
  3. If you are command-first, continue with hfSectAnalyzer Help and Commands.
  4. If you want a short look at runnable input/output flow, read Examples.
  5. If you need more background, read Theory.
  6. If you need repeatable or advanced control, move to Remote Control last.

docs.title: 1.3 Calculation of Sectional Constants for Arbitrary-Shaped Sections
docs.text:
• Calculates sectional constants such as area, second moment of area, centroid, torsional constant, and shear area.
  • The torsional constant and shear area are calculated through finite element analysis of a 2D potential problem.
  • After modeling the section with hf2DStudio, a finite element mesh is generated, and sectional constants are calculated.

Fig. 1. Computation of Sectional Constants

docs.title: 1.4 Nonlinear Sectional Analysis for Arbitrary-Shaped Sections
docs.text:
• Nonlinear sectional analysis can be performed for various cross-sections such as reinforced concrete or prestressed concrete beams or columns, and FRP-strengthened beams or columns.
  • The supported material models include linear elasticity, plasticity, and concrete. For plasticity and concrete models, the failure envelope can be defined using predefined functions or multiple linear conditions specified in a table.

  • The types of nonlinear sectional analysis that can be performed are as follows:

    • Analysis to find the corresponding axial strain and curvature for a given axial force and moment (NM analysis)
    • Analysis to find the corresponding axial strain and moment for a given axial force and curvature (NK analysis)
    • Analysis to find the corresponding axial force and curvature for a given axial strain and moment (EM analysis)
    • Analysis to find the corresponding axial force and moment for a given axial strain and curvature (EK analysis)

  • These analyses can be performed sequentially, and pretension and post-tension forces can be applied.

Fig. 2 illustrates the concept of deriving the moment-curvature curve by setting the axial force to zero and performing NK analysis. The PM diagram necessary for section design can be obtained by calculating the moment-curvature curves under various axial force conditions and determining the moment at failure (i.e., the maximum moment) (see Fig. 3).

Fig. 2. Nonlinear Sectional Analysis

Fig. 3. Computation of PM Diagram

docs.title: 2.7.1 Background
docs.text:
• Domain meshing in hf2DStudio uses built-in TFI and the external Netgen module together.
  • TFI (Transfinite Interpolation) works on a 4-side patch. The face boundary must be organized into four side chains, and the opposite side chains must have matching seed/sample counts. When this succeeds, TFI generates Q4 or Q8 elements directly, depending on the current mesh order.
  • Netgen is an external 2D mesher. Its natural result is triangular meshing. Depending on the mesh options, the generated triangles can later be merged into a quad-dominated mesh.
  • In practice, the automatic mesher tries to obtain clean Q4 meshing with TFI when possible, and otherwise falls back to Netgen.

docs.title: 2.7.2 Use TFI If Possible
docs.text:
When Settings > Mesh Generation Option > Use TFI if possible (Generate Q4 elements if possible) is enabled, Auto Mesh first tries to build a TFI boundary plan for each face before falling back to Netgen.

The current algorithm is:

  1. The face must have one outer loop and at least 4 curves.
  2. If the face already has Quad Mesh Corner Hints, the mesher uses those four outer-loop join points first. The internal side chains are ordered along the outer loop.
  3. If there are no hints, the mesher tries automatic corner detection. It evaluates the turning angle at each outer-loop join. Large positive turns (>= 30 deg) are treated as hard corners, and the other joins must stay nearly smooth (|angle| <= 15 deg).
  4. If there are no hints and the loop has 16 curves or fewer, the mesher also checks candidate combinations of four outer-loop join points.
  5. Once candidate corners are available, the boundary is divided into four side chains. One logical side may contain several connected curves.
  6. Each side chain is sampled with seedPoints() regardless of curve type, so lines, arcs, bezier curves, and splines all follow the same interval matching rule.
  7. If the opposite side chains have matching interval counts and the resulting TFI grid cells are valid, built-in TFI is used and quad elements are generated with the current mesh order.
  8. If there is not exactly one valid candidate, or if any check fails, the face falls back to Netgen.

So Use TFI if possible does not force TFI at all costs. It means "try TFI first, and if the face is not a valid TFI patch, continue with Netgen".

docs.title: 2.7.3 Auto Seed And TFI Interval Correction
docs.text:
Geometry > Auto seed and Remote Control auto-seed first run a rough seed pass that matches the selected curves by max-H. They then conservatively try TFI interval correction where possible.

  • Correction applies only to hole-free single-outer-loop faces whose outer-loop curves are all included in the current Auto Seed target set.
  • If the face has Quad Mesh Corner Hints, the hint plan is used first. Automatic corner candidates are used only when there are no hints.
  • Correction only increases seeds on deficient sides. The per-face budget is min(4, max(1, ceil(totalSideIntervals * 0.20))).
  • Seed changes are accepted only when exactly one valid TFI candidate remains after correction. If there are no valid candidates or multiple candidates, the rough seeds are kept.

Mesh generation itself does not change seeds. Auto Mesh and make-mesh build read the stored seeds and Quad Mesh Corner Hints, then choose either TFI or Netgen.

docs.title: 2.7.4 Enable Quadrilateral-Dominated Meshing
docs.text:
When Settings > Mesh Generation Option > Enable quadrilateral-dominated meshing (Convert T3 to Q4 if possible) is enabled, the Netgen path requests a quad-dominated result instead of a purely triangular one.

  • This option affects faces that are meshed by Netgen.
  • Netgen still starts from a triangle-oriented 2D mesher, so the result is not guaranteed to be all Q4.
  • When the boundary and local topology allow it, Netgen merges suitable T3 regions into quadrilateral elements and leaves the remaining parts as triangles.
  • If built-in TFI succeeds first, that face already receives direct Q4 elements from TFI, so this option mainly matters on fallback faces or when TFI is disabled.

This option is best understood as "prefer more quads in the Netgen result", not as "force every face to become a pure quad mesh".

docs.title: 2.7.5 Why Corner Hints Are Useful
docs.text:
Automatic corner detection is not always enough. Typical difficult cases are:

  • one logical side is split into several connected curves
  • rounded or smooth corners make the boundary look less explicit
  • the shape is visually quadrilateral, but the automatic detector cannot identify four reliable corners

Quad Mesh Corner Hints are face-level guidance for those cases. They let you keep the normal Auto Mesh workflow while telling the mesher which four outer-loop points should be treated as the TFI corners.

docs.title: 2.7.6 What A Hint Stores
docs.text:
A Quad Mesh Corner Hint is a set of four point ids stored on one face.

  • the four points must be distinct
  • all four points must be outer-loop join points of the same face
  • the entered order affects only the stored hint marker numbers; the actual side chains are ordered along the outer loop

Internally, the hint is stored as point ids, not as temporary picked coordinates.

docs.title: 2.7.7 How To Enter Hints
docs.text:
You can edit or clear hints when exactly one face is selected in the editable left view:

  • Geometry > Quad Mesh Corner Hints...
  • Geometry > Clear Quad Mesh Corner Hints
  • Geometry toolbar buttons
  • Model Tree face context menu
  • Section view face context menu

Open Quad Mesh Corner Hints... to start one editing session for the selected face.

  • type p1, p2, p3, p4 in the single input field, or click corners directly in the view
  • Apply validates the hint and closes the dialog on success
  • Close closes the session without applying pending changes
  • Backspace removes the last picked corner while picking is active
  • Esc cancels the picking session

docs.title: 2.7.8 Visual Feedback
docs.text:
Faces with stored hints are shown with a lightweight overlay in the section view:

  • numbered corner markers 1..4
  • a dashed polygon that connects the stored corners

The visibility of this stored overlay can be controlled from:

  • Settings > Display Geometric Entity > Quad Mesh Corner Hints

During active editing, the target face still shows pending corners and hover feedback for the next selectable join point.

docs.title: 2.7.9 Practical Workflow
docs.text:
The recommended workflow is:

  1. Enable Use TFI if possible (Generate Q4 elements if possible) when you want TFI-based Q4 meshing.
  2. Enable Enable quadrilateral-dominated meshing (Convert T3 to Q4 if possible) when you also want the Netgen fallback to prefer more quadrilateral elements.
  3. Run Auto seed on the full boundary curve set of each face intended for TFI.
  4. Run Auto Mesh or make-mesh build.
  5. If a face still falls back to Netgen, or the result is not the intended quad patch, add Quad Mesh Corner Hints to that face and mesh again.

This keeps the normal workflow simple and uses hints only on faces where automatic interpretation is ambiguous.

docs.title: 2.7.10 Related Pages
docs.text:
• hf2DStudio Help
  • Geometry
  • Geometry Remote Control

docs.title: 3.1 hfSectAnalyzer Help
docs.text:
hfSectAnalyzer is the sectional-analysis CLI solver in the 2D Modeling and Section Tools workflow.

Use it when you:

  • already know the section command syntax
  • want repeatable batch calculations
  • prefer command-driven section analysis over GUI-first editing

docs.title: 3.1.1 Relationship to hf2DStudio
docs.text:
• hf2DStudio is the 2D modeling and sectional-analysis GUI workspace.
  • hfSectAnalyzer is the command-line execution side for section calculations.
  • In practice, many users prepare the .hf2d model in the GUI first and then deepen into commands only when they need repeatable or solver-side work.

docs.title: 3.1.2 Recommended path
docs.text:
1. Read Section Overview to understand the roles of the two section programs.
  2. If you are GUI-first, start with hf2DStudio Help.
  3. If you are command-first, continue with Commands.
  4. Use Theory and Examples while validating your setup.

docs.title: 3.2.1 General Information
docs.text:
The input files used in hfSectAnalyzer/hf2DStudio are text files with blocks containing keywords, similar to those used in hfAnalyzer/hfStudio. The # character denotes a comment, and anything after it is ignored. Blank lines are also ignored. Other than the name following the Name keyword, the input is not case-sensitive. The canonical section-model extension is .hf2d.

Keywords used include *Environment, *Function, *Material, *Section, *SectionStop, *SectionSignal, *SectionAnalysis, and more. Among these, *Function, *Material, and *Section are commands shared with hfAnalyzer, while the rest are commands specific to hfSectAnalyzer/hf2DStudio.

*Environment, Type=UnitSystem
 force-length-time-temperature

*Function, TYPE=type, Name=name
...

*Material, TYPE=UGeneric, Name=name
...

*Geometry, Name=name
 ...

*Section, TYPE=Beam, Name=name
 *CellMeshPoint
  ...
 *Cell, TYPE=Recta


*SectionStop
  material, min_strain, max_strain  
  ...

*SectionSignal
  material, strain, msg
  ...

*SectionAnalysis, Name=name, Section=section,Left|Right Ref=angle,yp,zp, Output=Preselect|All
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=a,b,EK|EM|NK|NM, Inc=inc
  InitialStress|Stress, cellId, value
  ...
 *SectionStep, ...
  ...
 *SectionStepPM, MaxDeform=maxAxial,maxKappa, Inc=1000, PMPoints=50

*SectionAnalysis, Name=name, Section=section
...

The extension of the input file is not mandatory, but the canonical workflow uses .hf2d. Once analysis is performed, a log file and an .xlsx file are generated. The log file displays the calculation progress along with the computed section properties. The .xlsx file stores the results of nonlinear section analysis if *SectionAnalysis is present. For example, analyzing RCColumn.hf2d will result in RCColumn.xlsx containing the nonlinear section analysis results, and the process can be reviewed in the RCColumn.log file.

docs.title: 3.2.2 *Environement, TYPE=UnitSystem
docs.text:
This specifies the unit system. If this command is not present, it indicates that no units are used. The following units are available:

  • force: N, kN, kgf, tonf, lbf, kip
  • length: m, cm, mm, km, in, ft, yd, mi
  • time: s, min, hr, day
  • temperature: K, C, F

hfSectAnalyzer and hf2DStudio use the same 4-field global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem syntax as hfAnalyzer and hfStudio.

docs.title: 3.2.3 *Function
docs.text:
Defines functions required for material model definitions. Among the various functions defined in hfAnalyzer, only the following types can be used:

*Function, TYPE=Multilinear/ParabolaCEnv/HognestadCEnv/EC2CEnv/MPPCEnv/MaekawaTEnv/ConcreteTime

For detailed input, refer to the shared *Function command manual. Concrete envelope functions can use concrete material DB items, but the allowed standards depend on the function type. ParabolaCEnv is section-analysis input and accepts only KDS-2026-C<fck> and EC2-2004-C<fck>; it may include alpha before ToDirectForm. HognestadCEnv accepts KDS-2026-C<fck>, ACI318-2025-C<fck>, and EC2-2004-C<fck>. EC2CEnv accepts KDS-2026-C<fck> and EC2-2004-C<fck>. MPPCEnv and MaekawaTEnv accept KDS-2026-C<fck>, ACI318-2025-C<fck>, and EC2-2004-C<fck>. DB function input uses the current global unit system and does not allow a local UnitSystem=... keyword. HognestadCEnv, EC2CEnv, and MPPCEnv may include EciCurve before ToDirectForm. ConcreteTime supports both user-defined function references and EC2/KDS/ACI standard datalines. The user-defined form does not require a global UnitSystem, but standard datalines require the current global UnitSystem and do not allow a local UnitSystem=... keyword.

docs.title: 3.2.4 *Material
docs.text:
Defines a uniaxial material model. Among the various material models defined in hfAnalyzer, only the following types can be used. Properties such as Poisson's ratio, density, and thermal expansion coefficient are ignored.

*Material, TYPE=IsoElasticity/vonMises/UGeneric/USteel

For detailed input, refer to the shared *Material command manual. UGeneric does not take a concrete DB item directly in the material data lines. Define the concrete compression and tension envelope functions first, then reference those function names from UGeneric. Compression and tension envelopes may have different initial slopes; UGeneric uses each referenced function as entered.

docs.title: 3.2.5 *Geometry
docs.text:
*Geometry is an editable top-level geometry block written as *Geometry, Name=<name>. In the canonical .hf2d workflow, it is paired with *Section, TYPE=Beam, Name=<same-name> through the shared name. hf2DStudio uses it as the source 2D section sketch for drawing, face/rebar editing, and mesh generation. hfSectAnalyzer reads the same .hf2d file but ignores this block during analysis, so the actual analysis still depends on the generated *CellMeshPoint and *Cell data.

The *Geometry command line carries the geometry name and optional taper flag, but no direct data lines. The geometry itself is described through nested blocks such as *Point, *Curve, *Face, *FaceHint, and *Rebar. After meshing in hf2DStudio, the paired *Section, TYPE=Beam block stores the generated direct section mesh. Depending on the current mesh order and mesher path, the resulting *Cell, TYPE=Mesh connectivity can be T3, Q4, T6, or Q8.

*Geometry, Name=RectRC
 *Point
  ...
 *Curve
  ...
 *Face, 1, conc
  ...
 *FaceHint, 1, 11, 12, 13, 14
 *Face, 2, conc
  ...
 *FaceHint, 2, 21, 22, 23, 24
 ...
 *Rebar, 1, rebar, 25
  ...
 *Rebar, 2, rebar, 25
  ...

*Section, TYPE=Beam, Name=RectRC
 *CellMeshPoint
  ...
 *Cell, TYPE=Mesh
  ...

In practice, read this block as one *Point block and one *Curve block followed by as many *Face, *FaceHint, and *Rebar blocks as needed. *Point defines geometry points, *Curve defines the boundary curves, *Face defines closed regions and materials, *FaceHint optionally adds four quad-mesh corner hints to a corresponding face, and *Rebar defines reinforcing-bar groups based on geometry points. For taper sections, the left and right coordinates stay linked through the same geometry point entry. After meshing in hf2DStudio, the final analysis section is written as *CellMeshPoint and *Cell.

The nested blocks and their meaning are:

docs.title: 3.2.5.1 *Point
docs.text:
*Point
 id, y, z {, y, z}  
 ...

One point per data line. Point IDs must be unique inside the *Geometry block. For taper sections, one line stores the left and right coordinates of the same point so the linked geometry remains consistent. The trailing y, z pair is defined only for tapered sections.

docs.title: 3.2.5.2 *Curve
docs.text:
*Curve
 id, Line, seed, startPoint, endPoint
 id, Arc, seed, startPoint, middlePoint, endPoint
 id, Bezier, seed, point0, point1, point2[, w1]
 id, Bezier, seed, point0, point1, point2, point3[, w1, w2]
 id, Spline, seed, point1, point2, ..., pointN
seed is the mesh subdivision count used along the curve. Line uses 2 point IDs, Arc uses 3 point IDs (start, mid, end), quadratic Bezier uses 3 point IDs, cubic Bezier uses 4 point IDs, and Spline uses 2 or more point IDs. Arc requires three distinct non-collinear point IDs. Rational bezier curves use the same Bezier keyword with one optional inner weight for degree 2 or two optional inner weights for degree 3. For a 3-point section Bezier, omitting w1 keeps the legacy section-curve interpretation (w1 = 1/sqrt(2)). If you want a pure quadratic bezier, write w1 = 1.0 explicitly. When one weight is present, write it as a real-number token such as 1.0 or 0.70710678; a bare integer token is interpreted as the fourth point ID of a cubic bezier. For a 4-point Bezier, omitted weights are treated as unit weights. All referenced points must already be defined in *Point.

docs.title: 3.2.5.3 *Face
docs.text:
*Face, faceId, material
 +curve1, +curve2, -curve3, ...
 [additional loop lines if needed]
The command line defines the face ID and material name. Each following data line defines one closed loop with signed curve IDs. + uses the stored curve direction and - reverses it. Additional loop lines can be used for inner holes.

docs.title: 3.2.5.4 *FaceHint
docs.text:
*FaceHint, faceId, p1, p2, p3, p4
Defines four optional quad-mesh corner hints for an already defined face. The command is keyed by faceId, so it is an independent geometry command rather than a sub-line of *Face, even though it is usually written right after the matching face for readability. p1..p4 must be four distinct point IDs on the face's outer-loop join points. When TFI meshing is enabled, the mesher uses these hints before automatic corner detection to guide the four corners of the TFI patch. Linear mesh generation produces Q4 elements from that patch, while quadratic mesh generation produces Q8 elements.

docs.title: 3.2.5.5 *Rebar
docs.text:
*Rebar, rebarId, material, diameter[, diameterRight]
 pointId1, pointId2, ...
 [additional point lines if needed]
The command line defines the rebar group ID, material name, and bar diameter. Each following data line lists the geometry point IDs where rebars are placed. For taper sections, diameterRight can also be given.

  • Count rules Only one *Point block and one *Curve block are allowed in one *Geometry block. *Face, *FaceHint, and *Rebar blocks may appear multiple times.

docs.title: 3.2.6 *Section, TYPE=Beam
docs.text:
Among the various section types defined in hfAnalyzer, the Beam type can be used here. Related subcommands include *CellMeshPoint and *Cell.

For meshed sections, hf2DStudio now writes the direct mesh connectivity as generated. In other words, the *Cell, TYPE=Mesh block is not restricted to linear T3/Q4 cells. The same section block can contain T3, Q4, T6, or Q8 cells that share one *CellMeshPoint table.

docs.title: 3.2.6.1 *CellMeshPoint
docs.text:
*CellMeshPoint
 pointId, y, z {, y, z}
 ...

The trailing y, z pair is defined only for tapered sections.

docs.title: 3.2.6.2 *Cell
docs.text:
These commands are the same as in hfAnalyzer, but the available *Cell types are as follows.

*Cell, TYPE=Point/*Cell, TYPE=Point,Circle
*Cell, TYPE=Layer/*Cell, TYPE=Layer,Circle,/*Cell, TYPE=Layer,Stack
*Cell, TYPE=H/T/C/L/2C/2L/HR[-YUp]
*Cell, TYPE=Mesh/*Cell, TYPE=Mesh,Circle/*Cell, TYPE=Mesh,Rectangle
*Cell, TYPE=Mesh,H/T/C/L/2C/2L/HR[-YUp]

TYPE=H/T/C/L/2C/2L/HR[-YUp] defines a direct standard steel shape cell, is treated as a ShapeSection, and can use only elastic material (IsoElasticity). TYPE=Mesh,H/T/C/L/2C/2L/HR[-YUp] creates a real material point mesh from the same standard shape data, is treated as a MeshedSection, and can use elastic or inelastic material like a normal Mesh cell. These standard-shape dimensions follow the hf2DStudio template-mesh convention. HR uses H, B, t, r; if r=0, both inner and outer corners are generated as sharp corners, and if r>0, the outer corner radius is r + t. The other standard shapes include only the B2, tf2, c, and r1 through r4 fields meaningful for that shape. Add -YUp to the shape token, for example H-YUp or Mesh,H-YUp, when the section height should follow the local y-direction. For the TYPE=Mesh,H/T/C/L/2C/2L/HR[-YUp] generation form, ToDirectForm can be appended to the first data line to save the generated mesh as normal *CellMeshPoint and *Cell, TYPE=Mesh data.

When TYPE=Mesh is used, each mesh-cell data line may reference 3, 4, 6, or 8 point IDs depending on the generated section mesh. The standard-shape template mesh may contain Q8 rectangular cells, T6 quarter-fillet cells, and HR annular-corner Q8 cells when r>0. T3/T6 cells use triangle ordering with corner nodes first and midside nodes after them. Q4/Q8 cells use quadrilateral ordering with corner nodes first and edge midside nodes after them. hf2DStudio preserves that connectivity when exporting the section block.

Section DB references are written as DB, item in place of the numeric geometry data line. Tapered sections may use another DB reference on the second data line. AISC16 items use AISC designation prefixes such as W/M/S/HP, WT/MT/ST, C/MC, L, 2L, HSS, and Pipe; KSD3502-2022 items use Hyfeast-oriented prefixes such as H-, T-, C-, 2C-, L-, and 2L-. For example, H items use the H-HxBxtwxtf form. Round AISC16 HSS and PIPE items use Circle; rectangular and square HSS items use HR or Mesh,HR. Standard-shape DB references are preserved when saved or formatted unless a generated mesh cell uses ToDirectForm; Circle and Mesh,Circle DB references are saved as numeric circle data.

docs.title: 3.2.7 *SectionStop
docs.text: Specifies the strain at which the section analysis should stop for a particular material, if necessary.

docs.title: 3.2.8 *SectionSignal
docs.text: Specifies messages to output during section analysis for a particular material.

docs.title: 3.2.9 *SectionAnalysis
docs.text:
Specifies the section analysis. Subcommands include *SectionStep and *SectionStepPM. *SectionStep specifies the section analysis steps, and *SectionStepPM specifies the analysis steps to calculate the PM diagram.

*SectionStop includes data lines where you input the material, minimum strain (min_strain), and maximum strain (max_strain) at which the analysis should stop. *SectionSignal includes the material, strain condition (strain) at which to output the message, and the output message (msg). These two commands are optional. The following is an example:

*SectionStop
 conc,-0.005,
 rebar,-0.08,0.08

*SectionSignal
 conc, 0.0001042, "Concrete Tesile Failure"   
 rebar, 0.002, "Rebar Yield??

In *SectionAnalysis, Name represents the analysis name and is used as the basis for creating the sheet name in the .xlsx file. After Section=section, Left or Right specifies whether to use the start section or the end section when a tapered section is defined (default is Left). Ref=angle, yp, zp are the reference point and rotation angle (in degrees) (default is 0,0,0). In Output, specifying Preselect outputs stress and strain only at the top and bottom edges of each cell, while All outputs stress and strain at all material points (default is Preselect).

*SectionStep and *SectionStepPM are subcommands of *SectionAnalysis that specify the section analysis steps. *SectionStep refers to general section analysis specifying section deformations or forces. In ExtLoad, depending on the analysis type EK, EM, NK, NM, you specify the values a and b to be reached. Inc=inc is the number of increments, which is optional and defaults to 1.

  • ExtLoad=a,b,EK: Analyze until axial strain and curvature reach a and b, respectively.
  • ExtLoad=a,b,EM: Analyze until axial strain and moment reach a and b, respectively.
  • ExtLoad=a,b,NK: Analyze until axial force and curvature reach a and b, respectively.
  • ExtLoad=a,b,NM: Analyze until axial force and moment reach a and b, respectively.

The following example instructs to analyze in 100 increments until the curvature reaches 0.00004 while maintaining the axial force at 0:

*SectionAnalysis, Name=E1, Section=section
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=0.,0.00004,NK, Inc=100

*SectionStep can be specified consecutively, allowing for step-by-step section analysis. The following example applies an axial force up to 10, then varies the curvature while maintaining the axial force until failure:

*SectionAnalysis, Name=E1, Section=section
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=10.,0.,NM
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=10.,0.04,NK, Inc=100   # Assumption : 0.04 is large enough to fail the section

In the data lines of *SectionStep, you can specify initial stress (InitialStress) or target stress (Stress) for the cells that make up the section, if necessary. InitialStress specifies pretension, and Stress specifies post-tension. cellId is the ID of the cell, and value is the stress value. For example, InitialStress, 2, 1000 means to start the analysis with an initial stress of 1000 in cell 2. Stress, 3, 1000 means that cell 3 should have a stress state of 1000 at the final step of the analysis. Specifying Stress, 1, 0 effectively removes cell 1. The following is an analysis where pretension is applied to cell 2, then axial force is applied, and then curvature is applied until failure:

*SectionAnalysis, Name=PHC500A-N2 Section=PHC500A
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=0.,0.,NM, Inc=1
   InitialStress, 2, 994.625  # 0.7*fpu
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=-1766000,0,NM, Inc=1  
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=-1766000,0.02/250,NK, Inc=1000

The results of *SectionStep performed within *SectionAnalysis are saved in the sheet named Name in the .xlsx file. The output file has columns like step number, axial strain and axial force (Ex and Nx), curvature and bending moment (Kz, Mz), strain and stress at the material points of the cells (E.C1.1, S.C1.1, etc.), message (Msg.), and so on:

step, Ex, Nx, Kz, Mz, E.C1.1, S.C1.1, ..., Msg.
...

docs.title: 3.2.10 *SectionStepPM
docs.text:
*SectionStepPM is a command for analyzing the PM diagram. Internally, section analysis is performed by changing the axial force level. First, it calculates the failure load when only axial force is applied, using maxAxial as the axial strain value to be applied. Therefore, maxAxial should be a sufficiently large value that can cause compressive failure. Based on the axial failure load, failure analysis is performed while lowering the axial force level. pmpoints refers to the points on the PM diagram, i.e., the axial force levels. maxKappa defines the maximum curvature in each failure analysis, so it should be specified as a sufficiently large value to cause failure. Inc is the number of increments used in each failure analysis. The following is an example of performing PM analysis on a reinforced concrete section:

*SectionAnalysis, Name=RCSec, Section=RCSec
 *SectionStepPM, MaxDeform=-0.005,0.02/250, Inc=1000, PMPoints=50

You can specify *SectionStepPM only once within *SectionAnalysis, and it can be specified after *SectionStep but must be the final analysis step. The following is an example of performing PM analysis on a pretensioned member:

*SectionAnalysis, Name=PHC500A Section=PHC500A
 *SectionStep, ExtLoad=0.,0.,NM, Inc=1
   InitialStress, 2, 994.625  # 0.7*fpu
 *SectionStepPM, MaxDeform=-0.005,0.02/250, Inc=1000, PMPoints=50

*SectionStepPM performs as many section analyses as the number of PMPoints. The results of each section analysis are saved in sheets named Name-PM@plevel, and the deformation/forces at failure points are summarized and saved in the sheet Name-PM. In the above example, since PMPoints=50, the following files are generated:

  • PHC500A-PM@0: when the axial force level is 0
  • PHC500A-PM@2: when the axial force level is 2% of the failure axial force
  • ...
  • PHC500A-PM@100: when the axial force level is 100% of the failure axial force (moment is 0)
  • PHC500A-PM: file summarizing the deformation/forces at failure according to axial force levels

The Name-PM sheet has the following format:

PuLevel, ISTEP,Increment,E,N,K,M,MsgAtMaxPoint,RunningResultMsg
100,2,550,-0.002808,-8827490.751676,0.000000,-0.000000,,Stop Strain Reached
...

This axial force and flexural analysis was performed for a column cross-section with seismic details. The concrete strength is 24 MPa, and 36-D25 SD300 rebars were used. The confinement pressure of the confined concrete was assumed to be 1.5 MPa, from which the maximum strength (fccp) is calculated to be 30 MPa, and the maximum strain is assumed to be 0.01.
