docs.title: 3.1 Running hfAnalyzer
docs.text: hfAnalyzer is the finite-element CLI solver in Hyfeast. It reads a text .inp input file, runs the analysis, and writes run logs, text output, and result databases that hfStudio can open.

docs.title: 3.1.1 When to Use It
docs.text:
Use hfAnalyzer when solver execution itself is the main task.

  • You author or review .inp files directly.
  • You need repeatable batch runs.
  • You want a solver-centered workflow for verification or automation.
  • You want to control input through the command reference.

A brand-new GUI-first user usually starts with hfStudio Help or Tutorial Overview. Exact command syntax lives in Command Reference.

docs.title: 3.1.2 Basic Invocation
docs.text:
Pass the input file directly.

hfAnalyzer frame.inp

Use -h for the option list.

hfAnalyzer -h

Start without arguments for interactive entry of the input file and options.

hfAnalyzer

docs.title: 3.1.3 Parameters and Output Names
docs.text:
Use -p on the command line to apply parameter substitutions.

hfAnalyzer example.inp -p "<E>=20E9, <BaseN>=1000"

Defining *Parameter at the top of the input file lets you select named sets from the command line.

hfAnalyzer example.inp -p "Concrete"
hfAnalyzer example.inp -p "Steel"
hfAnalyzer example.inp -p "Concrete:<E>=30E9"

Use -o to change the default output base name.

hfAnalyzer example.inp -o output
hfAnalyzer example.inp -o "output-<PARAMETER>" -p "WT"

docs.title: 3.1.4 Checks and Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Before a run, check the model definition, intended steps and loads, and input-file revision. After a run, first check whether the run ended normally, whether warnings or errors appeared, and whether the expected output files were created.

When something fails, inspect these in order:

  • .log
  • .chk
  • .prn
  • the most recent modeling change
  • the related command definitions

When a large model does not work, reduce it to one or two elements and a single step. A smaller reproducible model usually makes the cause much clearer. Output file types and roles are described in Files and Results.

docs.title: 3.1.5 See Also
docs.text:
• Files and Results
  • Command Reference
  • Modelling Convenience
  • Examples

docs.title: 3.2 Files and Results
docs.text: This page covers the input and output files you encounter around an hfAnalyzer run.

docs.title: 3.2.1 Input file .inp
docs.text:
The main finite-element input definition for hfAnalyzer.

  • contains modeling, loading, material, section, function, and analysis-step definitions
  • follows a command-block structure where each block starts with *

Block-level syntax lives in Command Reference.

docs.title: 3.2.2 Text files written right after a run
3.2.2.1 .log
docs.text:
The run log.

  • how far the run progressed
  • whether warnings or errors appeared
  • the path the solver took

docs.title: 3.2.2.2 .chk
docs.text:
The flattened input file as the solver received it.

  • inspect what the solver actually accepted
  • see the final form after *Include expansion
  • review include and parameter substitution
  • check that global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem is not duplicated

docs.title: 3.2.2.3 .prn
docs.text:
The text-style output file, normally written next to the .inp.

  • run status and whether the run finished
  • warnings and errors — a quick grep -i "error\|warning" works
  • whether per-step results match expectations
  • basic progress information showing how far the run got

Step-level result definitions are documented in Step Result.

docs.title: 3.2.3 Result database .hdb
docs.text:
The result database used for postprocessing.

  • open it in hfStudio for graphical review
  • it underpins step, frame, contour, and history inspection

Database structure is documented in HDB File Structure.

docs.title: 3.2.3.1 .hdb format variants
docs.text:
hfAnalyzer can write the result database in several formats.

Default HDF5 format:

frame.hdb
frame.log
frame.chk
frame-step1.rst
frame-step2.rst

Text format:

frame.text.hdb
frame.text.hdb.info
frame.text.hdb.inp
frame.log
frame.chk
frame-step1.rst
frame-step2.rst

Binary format:

frame.bin.hdb
frame.log
frame.chk
frame-step1.rst
frame-step2.rst

docs.title: 3.2.4 Restart files -step*.rst
docs.text:
Per-step restart files.

  • relate to step-level restart and intermediate result flow
  • show up when an analysis runs with multiple steps or a long procedure

docs.title: 3.2.5 When to move to hfStudio
docs.text:
Use hfStudio for:

  • contour review
  • deformed shape inspection
  • step/frame browsing
  • scene-based result review

Details: hfStudio Help.

docs.title: 3.2.6 See also
docs.text:
• Running hfAnalyzer
  • Step Result
  • HDB File Structure

docs.title: 2.1 Overview
docs.text:
hfStudio is the finite-element GUI workspace of Hyfeast. It builds the model, runs the analysis, and reviews results from one window.

The main window is divided into central views, the Model Tree on the left, Command/Selection docks on the right, and the Output Window at the bottom. Menus and toolbars usually expose the same commands as different entry points; actual input and review continue in the workspace panels.

docs.title: 2.1.1 Two modes
docs.text:
The same program switches between two modes.

  • Preprocessing: define and edit the model (nodes, elements, materials, sections, loads, steps). Entered with a new model or an unlocked model.
  • Postprocessing: step, frame, contour, history review. Entered after analysis or by opening a result file.

Most definition and edit commands work only in preprocessing. Some actions change text and behavior with mode (for example, the single Analysis menu button becomes Unlock model in postprocessing).

docs.title: 2.1.2 Main screen areas
docs.text:
• Central views: the middle area. In addition to render views, you can place Node Table, Element Table, and Chart as tabs or splits.
  • Model Tree (left): structure tree of objects in the current model. Per-item visibility checkboxes are also here.
  • Command dock (right): panel where definition and edit widgets open.
  • Selection dock (right): selection mode, picking, Show/Hide, reset.
  • Output Window (bottom): import warnings, analysis log, failure causes.
  • Top menus: File / Display / Select / Preprocessing / Analysis / Postprocessing / View / Help.
  • Toolbars: File / Display / Selection / Postprocessing / Analysis (each toggleable).

Each area is detailed in the following GUI Guide pages.

  • File — file menu and toolbar (New, Open, Save, Import, Export, Write Scene/Program Shot, Quit)
  • View and Display — central view management; View menu (dock/toolbar visibility); Display menu (representation, projection, shading, display control, view direction, tool)
  • Selection and Visibility — selection kinds and modes, picking, Show/Hide, ModelTree checkboxes
  • Preprocessing — definition widgets, Node/Element editing, Assign to Selection, Model generator, Renumber
  • Analysis — Check Model, Run Analysis, Unlock model
  • Postprocessing — step/frame, contour, vector, deformed, animation, record
  • Workspace Panels — Model Tree, Render View, Command Panel, Selection Dock, Output Window, Node/Element Table, Chart

docs.title: 2.1.3 Relationship to Remote Control
docs.text:
GUI actions and Remote Control commands are 1:1.

  • For the same action, GUI Apply and Remote Control record the same canonical tail into history and *.ipc.txt.
  • The Remote Control manual defines validation rules, failure codes, and JSON response structures precisely for each command.
  • Each GUI Guide page cross-links to the matching Remote Control section per action.

For an automation primer, see Remote Control Basics. For the command reference, see Remote Control hfStudio Overview.

docs.title: 2.1.4 When hfAnalyzer fits better
docs.text:
The following are better handled in hfAnalyzer than in the GUI.

  • The .inp file is the main source of truth.
  • Repeatable batch runs are the center of the work.
  • You need precise control of solver syntax or parameter substitution options.

docs.title: 2.2 File
docs.text:
The hfStudio File menu and File toolbar create models, open and save them, exchange data with other formats, and close the program.

For automation of the same actions, see Remote Control File.

docs.title: 2.2.1 Menu layout
docs.text:
• New: Start a new empty model
  • Open: Open an existing model file
  • Save: Save to the current file
  • Save As: Save to a different path
  • Write Scene: Write the active render scene to an image or vector file
  • Write Program Shot: Capture the full program window as an image
  • Import from File: Import an external model file into the current model
  • Import from Clipboard: Import clipboard text into the current model
  • Export to File: Export the current model to an external format
  • Open Folder: Open the directory of the current file in the OS file explorer
  • Settings: Open the settings dialog
  • Exit: Quit the program

The File toolbar exposes New, Open, Import from File, Save, Write Scene, and Settings.

docs.title: 2.2.2 New
docs.text:
Start with an empty model.

If unsaved changes exist, a save-confirmation dialog appears.

  • Yes: Save the current model first. If there is no save path yet, the Save As dialog opens.
  • No: Discard unsaved changes and create a new empty model.
  • Cancel: Keep the current model open and abort the action.

Remote Control can skip this confirmation with --discard-unsaved.

Same action via Remote Control: new.

docs.title: 2.2.3 Open
docs.text:
Open the specified model file.

  • If unsaved changes exist and the current file already has a path, hfStudio auto-saves first.
  • If unsaved changes exist and the current file has no path, Open fails — there is no place to auto-save.

Same action via Remote Control: open.

docs.title: 2.2.4 Save / Save As
docs.text:
• Save: Save to the current file path. If there is no path, the Save As dialog opens automatically.
  • Save As: Pick a new path; that path is used for the save and becomes the current file path.

Remote Control collapses both into one command — save.

docs.title: Workspace root and .hyfeast
docs.text:
hfStudio stores runtime files such as Remote History, target metadata, replay input, and automatic backups under .hyfeast/ in the current workspace root. The workspace root follows the current model workflow rather than only the folder used to launch the program.

  • Opening a .hdb file switches the workspace root to that file's directory.
  • Saving with Save As switches the workspace root to the saved .hdb directory.
  • Importing an .inp into an empty model uses that .inp file's directory until the model is saved.
  • Export, Write Scene, Write Program Shot, and script file paths do not change the workspace root.
  • An Untitled model with no file keeps the current workspace root. If hfStudio starts without a file, the startup working directory is used.

docs.title: 2.2.5 Write Scene
docs.text:
Write the active render scene to an image or vector file.

Supported extensions:

  • raster: .png, .jpg, .bmp, .pnm, .tif
  • vector: .svg, .ps, .eps, .pdf, .tex

Same action via Remote Control: write-scene.

docs.title: 2.2.6 Write Program Shot
docs.text:
Capture the entire hfStudio program window — menu bar, toolbars, dock widgets, central views, and status bar — to an image file.

  • The parent directory of the output path must already exist.
  • The file extension must be a raster format supported by the current Qt image writer (.png, .jpg, etc.).
  • Vector formats such as .svg, .pdf, .ps, .eps, and .tex are not supported.

Comparison with Write Scene:

  • Write Scene: captures only the active render view; raster + vector both supported.
  • Write Program Shot: captures the entire program window; raster only.

Same action via Remote Control: write-program-shot.

docs.title: 2.2.7 Import from File / Import from Clipboard
docs.text:
Import an external model file or clipboard text into the current model.

Supported formats and extension inference:

  • Hyfeast: .inp
  • DXF: .dxf
  • MGT: .mgt
  • MCT: .mct
  • Abaqus: no extension inference (pick the format explicitly in the GUI)
  • GMSH: .msh

DXF import behavior:

  • ASCII DXF with line/polyline entities (LINE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE) is the documented guaranteed scope.
  • Binary DXF and version-specific advanced entities are outside the guaranteed scope.
  • DXF unit scaling applies only when both DXF $INSUNITS and the current DB/global UnitSystem are valid; otherwise coordinates come in as raw numbers.

Three .inp text ingest paths share the same UnitSystem rules:

  • File > Import from File
  • File > Import from Clipboard
  • The Apply button on the Inp Text dock

If *Include directives are present, they are expanded first and then the same rules apply:

  • If the host DB has a global *Environment, TYPE=UnitSystem and the imported text also has a global UnitSystem, imported values are converted to the host global before insertion.
  • If the host DB is empty and has no global UnitSystem, the imported root global UnitSystem is adopted before reading the text. This makes File > New followed by .inp import behave like opening the input file as a new model.
  • If the host DB already contains model data and has no global UnitSystem, the imported root global UnitSystem is not adopted into the host and the values come in as raw numbers without conversion.
  • *Function, UnitSystem=... and section-local UnitSystem are not stripped during import.

Same action via Remote Control: import.

docs.title: 2.2.8 Export to File
docs.text:
Export the current model to an external format. The output path and extension must be supported by the existing export flow.

Same action via Remote Control: export.

docs.title: 2.2.9 Open Folder
docs.text: Open the directory of the current file in the OS file explorer. Useful for quickly inspecting result files or side outputs.

docs.title: 2.2.10 Settings
docs.text: Open the settings dialog. Individual options are documented inside the dialog.

docs.title: 2.2.11 Exit
docs.text:
Quit the program.

  • If unsaved changes exist and the current file has a path, hfStudio auto-saves first.
  • If unsaved changes exist and the file has no path, Exit fails — there is no place to auto-save.
  • Remote Control can quit immediately without auto-save using --discard-unsaved.

Same action via Remote Control: quit.

docs.title: 2.2.12 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control File
  • hfAnalyzer Files and Results

docs.title: 2.3 View and Display
docs.text:
This page covers building the screen layout, aiming the camera, switching rendering representations, and toggling labels and measurement tools.

For automation of the same actions, see Remote Control View and Remote Control Display.

The Render View is the central workspace for viewing the model and results. The Display menu and Display toolbar change its representation, displayed items, camera direction, and measurement tools.

docs.title: 2.3.1 Central views and render views
docs.text:
The central area can hold multiple views as tabs or splits at the same time.

  • Render View: 3D view of the model and results. id: r0, r1, …
  • Node Table: node data table. id: n0, …
  • Element Table: element data table. id: e0, …
  • Chart: result chart. id: c0, …

Two key concepts:

  • currentView: the central view that currently has focus. It can be a table or chart, not just a render view.
  • activeRenderView: the render view that display, camera, and visibility commands target by default. Even when the currentView is not a render view, the last active render view is tracked separately.

Adding, activating, and closing views uses the GUI tab/split UI. The same actions are scriptable via Remote Control view.

The last remaining render view cannot be closed.

docs.title: 2.3.2 View menu — dock and toolbar visibility
docs.text:
The top-level View menu toggles dock widget and toolbar visibility. It is not a camera control.

Dock widgets:

  • Output Window
  • Model Tree
  • Command
  • Selection Widget
  • Chart Control Widget
  • Digital Twin Widget

Toolbars:

  • File
  • Display
  • Selection
  • Postprocessing
  • Analysis

The same toggles are reachable from each toolbar's right-click popup.

docs.title: 2.3.3.1 Representation submenu
docs.text:
Sets the rendering style for the target render view.

  • Wireframe: wireframe representation. RC: representation wireframe
  • Surface: surface representation. RC: representation surface
  • Transparency: toggle transparent rendering. RC: transparency
  • Shrink: toggle element shrink. RC: element-shrink
  • Section View: toggle section-view clipping. RC: section-view

Remote Control collapses the three representation modes (surface, wireframe, both) into one command.

docs.title: 2.3.3.2 Parallel Projection
docs.text:
Standalone toggle in the Display menu. Switches between perspective and parallel projection.

Same action via Remote Control: parallel-projection.

docs.title: 2.3.3.3 Shading Color submenu
docs.text:
• Shading by Element Type: RC value element-type
  • Shading by Section: RC value section

Automation: shading-color <none|element-type|section>.

docs.title: 2.3.3.4 Display Control submenu
docs.text:
Each item works in both preprocessing and postprocessing. Toggle command: display-control <item> <on|off>.

  • Origin Axes: RC <item> origin-axes
  • Corner Axes: corner-axes
  • Grid: grid
  • Auto Grid Spacing: separate command: grid-spacing set auto
  • Dimension Box: dimension-box
  • Node: node
  • Node Label: node-label
  • Element Label: element-label
  • ECS: ecs
  • Sensor Label: sensor-label

docs.title: 2.3.3.5 View Direction submenu
docs.text:
Quick camera changes for the target render view.

  • View Reset: default fit. RC: camera fit
  • Area Zoom: zoom to a screen-drawn rectangle (interactive only)
  • Iso Z/Y/X: isometric. RC: camera view iso-z|iso-y|iso-x
  • +X / −X / +Y / −Y / +Z / −Z: axis-aligned view. RC: camera view +x|-x|+y|-y|+z|-z
  • Rotate ±X/Y/Z: rotate the current camera. RC: camera rotate ±X|±Y|±Z
  • Set User View ½/3: save the current camera into a user-view slot (interactive only)
  • Unset User View ½/3: clear a user-view slot (interactive only)
  • User View ½/3: recall a saved user view (interactive only)

For exact position, focal point, and roll, use Remote Control camera set --position ... --focal-point ... --view-up ....

docs.title: 2.3.3.6 Tool submenu
docs.text:
Place measurement tools inside a render view.

  • Distance Tool: distance between two points
  • Angle Tool: angle defined by three points (p1, center, p2)
  • Clear Tools: remove all tool widgets from the current render view

Automation behavior:

  • Calling without coordinates enters interactive picking mode in the GUI.
  • Passing coordinates places a completed tool directly — Remote Control tool distance <p1> <p2>, tool angle <p1> <center> <p2>.
  • Rejected when another tool placement is in progress or the view is in a deformed state.
  • Clear Tools is active only when there is at least one tool to clear.

docs.title: 2.3.4 Grid spacing
docs.text:
The Auto Grid Spacing action in the Display menu and the Display toolbar adjusts spacing to fit the current work-plane view.

  • It changes the spacing value only; grid on/off state is left alone.
  • It does nothing when grid is off, or when an oblique view angle is hiding the work-plane grid.
  • For automation, history records the semantic tail grid-spacing set auto instead of the resolved number.

To set or query the value directly, use Remote Control grid-spacing.

docs.title: 2.3.5 Targeting another render view
docs.text: Remote Control commands accept --view-id <rN> to apply display, camera, or visibility changes to a specific render view without changing currentView or activeRenderView. In the GUI, the equivalent flow is to activate the target render view first.

docs.title: 2.3.6 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control View
  • Remote Control Display
  • Selection and Visibility

docs.title: 2.4 Selection and Visibility
docs.text:
Selection defines the set that the next command (edit, delete, assign, ...) will act on. Visibility changes the on-screen state of a render view without modifying the model.

For automation, see Remote Control Selection and the visibility command in Remote Control Display.

Model Tree checkboxes directly change visibility in the current render view. The Selection Dock and Selection toolbar expose selection kind, selection mode, picking, Show/Hide, and reset actions.

docs.title: 2.4.1 The two concepts
docs.text:
• Selection: defines the target set of the next edit/delete/assign command. Does not touch model data.
  • Visibility: shows or hides objects in a render view. Does not touch model data (per-view state).

ModelTree checkboxes toggle visibility directly. The Show/Hide actions in the Select menu change the same visibility state.

docs.title: 2.4.2 Selection kinds
docs.text:
Selection is tracked per kind. Mapped to RC select <kind>.

  • Node: node
  • Element: element
  • Constraint: constraint
  • Load: load
  • Spline: spline
  • Guide (construction line): guide
  • Surface: surface
  • Edge: edge
  • Sensor: sensor
  • Face: part of surface selection; no separate RC kind

Detailed input formats are in Remote Control select.

docs.title: 2.4.3 Selection toolbar and Selection dock
docs.text: The Selection dock and Selection toolbar on the right side of the window expose the most common selection actions — selection mode, picking modes, Show/Hide, and per-kind reset.

docs.title: 2.4.4.1 Selection Mode
docs.text:
Decides how a new selection combines with the current one. The chosen mode applies to subsequent picking until changed.

  • Current Selection: replace with the new selection. RC --mode current (default).
  • Union Selection: add to the current selection. RC --mode union.
  • Intersection Selection: keep only items in both. RC --mode intersection.
  • XOR Selection: keep only items in exactly one. RC --mode xor.
  • Prev Diff Cur Selection: current minus the new. RC --mode prev-diff-cur.
  • Cur Diff Prev Selection: new minus the current. RC --mode cur-diff-prev.

For automation, pass the matching mode to Remote Control select ... --mode <value>.

docs.title: 2.4.4.2 Select by Picking
docs.text:
• Surface Select Node: pick nodes on the clicked surface
  • Surface Select Element: pick elements on the clicked surface
  • Surface Select Face: pick faces on the clicked surface
  • Surface Select Edge: pick edges on the clicked surface
  • Frustum Select Node: multi-pick nodes inside a screen frustum
  • Frustum Select Element: multi-pick elements inside a screen frustum
  • Dynamic View: keep picking mode active during view rotate/pan

For automation, specify ids or names instead of picking. Inputs accepted by Remote Control select:

  • node, element — 1,2,3, 1:5, 1:9:2, none
  • constraint, load, spline, guide, sensor — name,name,... or none
  • surface — surfaceName, faceId@elementPattern, faceId@elsetName, none
  • edge — node-id chain such as 17-23 or 17-42-23, or none

select node and select element accept --ignore-missing so that absent ids are skipped (the command still fails with NOT_FOUND when none of the requested ids exist).

docs.title: 2.4.4.3 Select 2 (derived selection)
docs.text:
Build a new selection from existing ones.

  • Select Elements from Other Selections: extract the elements implied by other-kind selections
  • Select Nodes from Other Selections: extract the nodes implied by other-kind selections
  • Select Free Nodes: select nodes that no element references

docs.title: 2.4.4.4 Show/Hide (Visibility)
docs.text:
Toggle the on-screen state of the current node/element selection. The model itself is not changed.

  • Show Node/Element Selection: make the selected nodes/elements visible
  • Show Node/Element Selection Only: keep the selection visible and hide everything else
  • Hide Node/Element Selection: hide the selected nodes/elements

For automation, use Remote Control visibility:

visibility <node|element|node-set|element-set|constraint|load|surface|construction|sensor> <items|all> <on|off>
  • The command operates on the per-render-view state mirrored by ModelTree checkboxes, not on a global all-view visibility.
  • ModelTree checkbox changes also record the canonical visibility ... tail into Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.
  • construction covers both splines and guides by name.

docs.title: 2.4.4.5 Reset Selection
docs.text:
Clear the selection by kind.

  • All: call select <kind> none per kind
  • Node: select node none
  • Element: select element none
  • Face: select surface none or per-surface clearing
  • Edge: select edge none
  • Load: select load none
  • Constraint: select constraint none
  • Sensor: select sensor none
  • Guide: select guide none
  • Spline: select spline none

docs.title: 2.4.5 ModelTree checkboxes = per-view visibility
docs.text: Each item in the ModelTree on the left has a checkbox that toggles visibility for that object directly. To toggle many objects at once, build a selection and use Show/Hide.

docs.title: 2.4.6 Targeting another render view
docs.text: Adding --view-id <rN> to the Remote Control visibility command applies the change to a different render view without changing currentView or activeRenderView. In the GUI, the equivalent flow is to activate the target render view first.

docs.title: 2.4.7 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control Selection
  • Visibility command in Remote Control Display
  • View and Display

docs.title: 2.5 Preprocessing
docs.text:
This page covers the menus and dock widgets used to define and edit the model in preprocessing mode.

For automation, see Remote Control Preprocessing 2.7.x.

The Command Panel is the actual input area for preprocessing commands. Choosing an item from the Preprocessing menu opens the matching definition or edit widget in the right dock; Apply records the same canonical Remote Control tail into history and *.ipc.txt.

Node Table and Element Table are table-style edit views opened in the central area. They operate on the same model data as the menu commands, and row edits or deletions follow the same Remote Control rules.

docs.title: 2.5.1 Mode and model history
docs.text:
Most definition and edit commands work only in preprocessing mode. The following exception paths are still allowed in postprocessing mode to match the GUI: environment-info set, nset, elset, step Post ..., step-delete-from ..., history PostHistory ....

  • Undo: RC: undo. Fails with NOTHING_TO_UNDO.
  • Redo: RC: redo. Fails with NOTHING_TO_REDO.

undo/redo re-applies the in-memory model-history stack of the session, not a re-parse of input text. The result JSON includes canUndo and canRedo after the command is applied.

docs.title: 2.5.2 Definition widgets
docs.text:
Each menu item opens the corresponding definition dock or dialog. GUI Apply records the same canonical Remote Control tail into Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.

Definition commands that edit block text use the same body syntax as GUI Apply, and accept either --content <text> or --content-file <file>.

  • Coordinate System: coordinatesystem, -rename, -delete, coordinatesystem-activate
  • Construction: construction, -rename, -delete
  • Material: material, -rename, -delete
  • Section: section, -rename, -delete
  • Function: function, -rename, -delete
  • Load: load, -rename, -delete
  • Surface: surface
  • Sensor: sensor, -rename, -delete
  • NProp: nprop
  • Constraint: GUI widget only; in automation, constraints live in step content
  • Step: step, -rename, -delete, step-delete-from (postprocessing)
  • History: history, -rename, -delete
  • Environment: environment-info, environment-control (Environment)
  • Model: model <type> (model generator)

coordinatesystem-activate mirrors the TreeMenu check/uncheck flow for User coordinate systems on a render view. Pass a name to activate, or none to deactivate.

When the Function widget is set to Type=TimeSignal, it can open the DB record selection dialog. The dialog's Add Record... action checks a user-provided text or .npy time-history file, collects record name, quantity, UnitSystem, dtime, nseries, skipRows, and sourceScaleFactor metadata, and registers it as a user DB record. Registered records are stored in tools/db/timeSignal/user/catalog.yml and tools/db/timeSignal/user/files/, then inserted into the TimeSignal source lines as DB, recordName[, scaleFactor]. Before updating the program or replacing the installation folder, back up or copy the whole tools/db/timeSignal/user/ folder if those user records should be kept.

The Analyze... button opens the non-modal Signal Analysis window for the current TimeSignal definition. From the Function widget, the window can compare multiple series resolved from the TimeSignal source lines; from the TimeSignal DB dialog, it analyzes the selected DB record. A TimeSignal definition may contain mixed quantities such as acceleration, velocity, and displacement records. The Time History tab can display the original quantity, one selected quantity, or a three-row acceleration/velocity/displacement view. Derived histories are display-only and do not modify the source TimeSignal, DB record, or source file. The window provides Time History, FFT, Response Spectrum, Statistics, and Metadata tabs. FFT can optionally remove the mean before transform. Response Spectrum uses damping and period-range controls, can display pSa, Sa, or Sd, and can draw the x-axis as Period/Linear, Period/Log, Frequency/Linear, or Frequency/Log; it is computed from acceleration. Velocity and displacement sources are numerically differentiated to acceleration for this tab, while Other/dimensionless series are skipped. Statistics report the source series values and include min/max/mean/RMS values and acceleration-like measures such as PGA, Arias Intensity, and CAV when applicable. Plot export uses the JKQtPlotter toolbar graph/data export actions; toolbar data export follows the displayed plot data, so dense histories may be exported after plot decimation/envelope reduction.

Derived acceleration, velocity, and displacement histories use the same numerical rules as tools/eqsig.py. TimeSignal samples are stored at \(t_i=(i+1)\Delta t\) and imply zero at \(t=0\). For an input series \(x_i\), integration uses the trapezoidal rule

\[ I_0 = \frac{\Delta t}{2}x_0 \] \[ I_i = I_{i-1} + \frac{\Delta t}{2}\left(x_{i-1}+x_i\right), \qquad i=1,\ldots,N-1 \]

Differentiation uses the backward-difference rule

\[ D_0 = 0 \] \[ D_i = \frac{x_i-x_{i-1}}{\Delta t}, \qquad i=1,\ldots,N-1 \]

No baseline correction, drift correction, filtering, or window correction is applied during these displayed quantity conversions.

In the FFT tab, Display=Amplitude and Display=Power use the same transform result. For a time series with \(N\) samples and interval \(\Delta t\), mean removal first replaces the values by

\[ x'_m = x_m - \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} x_k \]

When mean removal is off, \(x'_m=x_m\). The plotted non-negative frequency points are

\[ f_i = \frac{i}{N\Delta t}, \qquad X_i = \Delta t\sum_{m=0}^{N-1} x'_m e^{-j2\pi mi/N}, \qquad i=0,\ldots,\left\lfloor \frac{N}{2}\right\rfloor \]

The amplitude spectrum displays

\[ A_i = |X_i| \]

and the power spectrum displays

\[ P_i = A_i^2 = |X_i|^2 \]

This Power Spectrum is a direct squared-amplitude display, not a power spectral density; it is not divided by frequency spacing and no window correction is applied.

docs.title: 2.5.3 Node menu / Node Table
docs.text:
The Node menu and the Node Table dock act on the same data.

  • Node Create: node <id> <x,y,z> [--nset] [--merge-node]
  • Node Copy (translate-copy / translate-move / rotate-copy / rotate-move) — node-copy
  • Node Delete (Node Table row delete) — node-delete <ids|__selected__>
  • Set Nodeset: nset <name> --content ..., -rename, -delete
  • Merge Node Tolerance: merge-node-tolerance get|set <value>

Merge Node Tolerance is shared session-wide and applies to node --merge-node on, node-copy, element-extrude, and element-divide.

docs.title: 2.5.4 Element menu / Element Table
docs.text:
• Element Create: element <type> <id> <n1,n2,...>
  • Element Update (Element Table edit) — element-update
  • Element Extrude (translate/rotate from current selection) — element-extrude
  • Element Divide (refine/topology/parametric) — element-divide
  • Element Change (retype/reverse-node-order/explode) — element-change
  • Element Copy: element-extrude --remove-source off
  • Element Delete (Element Table row delete) — element-delete <ids|__selected__>
  • Set Elementset: elset <name> --content ..., -rename, -delete
  • Delete Node/Element Selection (shortcut) — snapshot-based: records element-delete <ids> then node-delete <ids>

Partial-delete behavior: when safe delete leaves some items behind, the response is DELETE_PARTIAL with requestedIds, deletedIds, remainingIds, and a canonical scriptTail. The applied portion is recorded into history.

docs.title: 2.5.5 Assign to Selection
docs.text:
Collects the assign actions from the preprocessing context menu. The default target is the current element selection; --source <ids|__selected__> overrides it.

  • Assign Section: assign-section <section|none>
  • Assign Beam CS: assign-beam-cs <beamcs|none>
  • Assign Beam End Release: assign-beam-end-release <code|none>. code = combination of Rx1 / Ry1 / Rz1 / Rx2 / Ry2 / Rz2.
  • Assign Embedded Line Spline: assign-embedded-line-spline <spline|none>
  • Assign Embedded Line Host Elset: assign-embedded-line-host-elset <host-elset|none>
  • Assign MCK Element Scale Factor: assign-mck-element-scale-factor <value>. positive real value.
  • Assign MCK Element CS: assign-mck-element-cs <ucs|none>
  • Assign Moving Spring Initial Position: assign-moving-spring-initial-position <x,y>
  • Assign Shell Thickness, Shell Director: GUI only (element-property edit path)

Internally, each assign-* writes one *Distribution, TYPE=... block; clearing applies *Distribution, TYPE=..., Remove. There is no separate distribution remote command.

docs.title: 2.5.6 Model Generator
docs.text:
The Model widget builds a large mesh from a predefined shape generator.

  • Block2D, Block3D — rectangular block
  • Cylinder — cylinder
  • Wall — wall
  • RectangularTank, CylindericalTank — tank
  • CurveExtrusion — extrude along a curve
  • FarField2D, FarField3D, FarField2Dx, FarField3Dx — far-field boundary

Automation: model <type> --content ....

On apply, hidden items keep their per-view hidden state, new visible items are added to each view, topology is refreshed, and the camera is reset.

docs.title: 2.5.7 Renumbering
docs.text:
• Selected Nodes: renumber selected-nodes <start-id> <prio1> <prio2> <prio3>
  • Selected Elements: renumber selected-elements ...
  • All Nodes: renumber all-nodes ...
  • All Elements: renumber all-elements ...

Each priority token is one of +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z, and the three must be distinct. See Remote Control Renumber for details.

The selected modes require a non-empty current selection.

docs.title: 2.5.8 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control Preprocessing
  • Selection and Visibility
  • Analysis

docs.title: 2.6 Analysis
docs.text:
This page covers model checking, starting an analysis, and returning a result-bearing model to preprocessing mode.

For automation, see Remote Control Analysis.

The Output Window is where model import, check, and analysis messages are reviewed, including failure causes. Actions launched from the Analysis menu or Analysis toolbar report their result here.

docs.title: 2.6.1 Analysis menu
docs.text:
• Check Model: runs the existing validation path; render mode is left alone. RC: check-model.
  • Analysis (preprocessing) — starts the analysis. RC: run-analysis [--ncpu <n>].
  • Unlock model (postprocessing) — the same button changes to "Unlock model" in postprocessing. RC: unlock-model.

The Analysis action is one physical button whose text and icon switch with the current mode. The matching button on the Analysis toolbar behaves the same way.

docs.title: 2.6.2 Check Model
docs.text:
• Uses the existing validation path.
  • Does not change render mode.
  • Both GUI Apply and Remote Control record the same canonical check-model tail into history.

docs.title: 2.6.3 Run Analysis (Analysis)
docs.text:
• Starts the analysis from preprocessing mode.
  • Requires a saved current file path before starting.
  • If unsaved changes exist, both GUI and Remote Control attempt to save first.
  • Remote Control accepts --ncpu <n> to set the core count.

On success, records the same canonical run-analysis tail into history.

docs.title: 2.6.4 Unlock Model
docs.text:
• Works only in postprocessing mode.
  • Removes all result steps and returns to preprocessing mode.

On success, records the same canonical unlock-model tail into history.

docs.title: 2.6.5 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control Analysis
  • Postprocessing
  • Running hfAnalyzer

docs.title: 2.7 Postprocessing
docs.text:
This page covers stepping through results once the analysis is done — moving between steps and frames, controlling contour/vector/diagram/sensor/deformed display, and driving animation.

For automation, see Remote Control Postprocessing.

Postprocessing commands work only in postprocessing mode. post-* get queries return JSON and do not record a history tail. Setter commands record the same canonical post-* ... tail into Remote Control History and *.ipc.txt.

docs.title: 2.7.1 Plot toggles
docs.text:
Automation: post-plot <type> <on|off>.

  • Contour: RC value contour
  • Diagram: diagram
  • Vector: vector
  • Sensor Plot: sensor
  • Deformed: deformed

Deformed on fails when the current result step has no displacement output D.

docs.title: 2.7.2 Step and frame navigation
docs.text:
• Step pick (Step combobox) — RC: post-step <step-name>. Also moves to frame 1.
  • Query current step and frame: RC: post-step get, post-frame get.
  • Frame pick: RC: post-frame <index> (1-based).

The Postprocessing menu's Play submenu has frame-navigation buttons:

  • Follow Step Model: toggle: change the model shape with the step
  • First: first frame of the current step
  • Previous: previous frame
  • Next: next frame
  • Last: last frame

In automation, jump directly with post-frame <index> instead of stepping.

docs.title: 2.7.3 Scalar (Contour Field)
docs.text:
• Pick scalar field: RC: post-scalar <field> [<avg-threshold>]
  • Query current scalar: RC: post-scalar get

<field> must be a valid scalar field name for the current step and frame. [<avg-threshold>] is optional and accepts an integer in 0..100.

The GUI Averaging Threshold(%) controls whether extrapolated element scalar values are averaged at shared element nodes. 0 disables averaging, while 1..100 averages values in the same averaging group only when they satisfy:

\[ \max(v_i)-\min(v_i) \le \frac{\mathrm{threshold}}{100} \left(\max(v_\mathrm{region})-\min(v_\mathrm{region})\right) \]

Averaging groups are formed within the same section, and \(v_\mathrm{region}\) is the scalar value range of that section group. Continuum elements average by shared node. Shell elements keep bottom/top values separate and average only values with the same shell element coordinate system. Beam elements average only values with the same section/material point index and beam element coordinate system.

docs.title: 2.7.4 Vector / Tensor
docs.text:
• Pick vector or tensor field: RC: post-vector <field>
  • Query current vector: RC: post-vector get

docs.title: 2.7.5 Contour settings
docs.text:
Controls range, mode, levels, and overlay of the contour. Automation lives in the post-contour command family:

  • Auto-range toggle: post-contour auto-range <on|off>
  • Range value: post-contour range <min> <max>
  • Band count: post-contour bands <n>
  • Mode: post-contour mode <uniform|custom>
  • Custom levels: post-contour levels <v1,v2,...> (strictly increasing, 2..31 values)
  • Overlay text: post-contour overlay <text>
  • Overlay color: post-contour overlay-color <r,g,b[,a]> (0..255)

The auto-range, range, and bands setters are rejected in custom mode. Switching to mode custom initializes custom levels from the current uniform range and band state if needed.

docs.title: 2.7.6 Scale factor
docs.text:
Controls deformed shape, diagram, vector, and sensor scales. Automation: post-scale.

  • Deformed (auto on/off): post-scale deformed auto <on|off>
  • Deformed (explicit value): post-scale deformed value <scale>
  • Diagram: post-scale diagram auto, post-scale diagram value
  • Vector: post-scale vector auto, post-scale vector value
  • Sensor: post-scale sensor auto, post-scale sensor <e|d|v|a> <scale>

Passing an explicit value or e|d|v|a automatically turns the matching auto-scale off first.

docs.title: 2.7.7 Overlay and display
docs.text:
Automation: post-display <item> <on|off>.

  • Information (top-left info text) — RC <item> information
  • Scalar bar: scalarbar
  • Min/Max tag (captions) — min-max-tag

docs.title: 2.7.8 Play (animation)
docs.text:
Animation controls live under the Postprocessing menu's Play submenu and on the toolbar.

  • Time History Ani: step through frames. RC: post-animation-time-history <on|off>.
  • Scale Factor Ani: step through scale values. RC: post-animation-scale-factor <on|off>.
  • Loop: toggle automatic looping. RC: post-animation-loop <on|off>.
  • Record: record animation to .avi/.mp4. RC: post-animation-record <on|off> [<file>].

Animation rules:

  • Time History and Scale Factor cannot run at the same time (turning one on while the other is active is rejected).
  • Record on requires a writable output path with a .avi or .mp4 extension.
  • The record target can be changed only while no animation is running.

docs.title: 2.7.9 See also
docs.text:
• Remote Control Postprocessing
  • Analysis
  • Selection and Visibility

docs.title: 2.8 Workspace Panels
docs.text: In hfStudio, menus and toolbars are command entry points. State review, input, and result inspection happen in the workspace panels. This page describes the screen areas without repeating every menu item.

docs.title: 2.8.1 Main Window Map
docs.text:
• Top menu / toolbar strip: entry points for File, Display, Selection, Preprocessing, Analysis, Postprocessing, and View commands.
  • Model Tree: model object structure and per-view visibility state.
  • Central views: workspace area for Render View, Node Table, Element Table, and Chart tabs or splits.
  • Command / Selection dock: right-side command input and selection-control panels.
  • Output Window: log area for import, check, analysis, and Remote Control messages.

docs.title: 2.8.2 Top Menu and Toolbar Strip
docs.text: Menus and toolbars usually expose the same features. Menus show the full command list and grouping; toolbars provide faster access to common commands. Toolbar visibility is controlled from the View menu.

docs.title: 2.8.3 Model Tree
docs.text: The Model Tree groups the objects in the current model by type. Its checkboxes do not delete or edit model data; they only change visibility in the current render view. To show or hide many items at once, build a selection first and use the Select menu's Show/Hide actions.

docs.title: 2.8.4 Render View
docs.text: The Render View is the central 3D view for model geometry, display items, and analysis results. Display menu and Display toolbar commands such as representation, projection, shading, labels, grid, camera, and measurement tools target the active render view by default.

docs.title: 2.8.5 Command Panel
docs.text:
The Command Panel is the actual input area for definition and edit commands. Choosing Environment, Coordinate System, Node, Element, Material, Section, Function, Step, History, or Model from the Preprocessing menu opens the matching widget in the right dock.

Pressing Apply or Apply & Close converts GUI input into the canonical Remote Control tail and records it into history and *.ipc.txt. When a manual workflow needs to be automated, reuse that recorded command as the starting point.

docs.title: 2.8.6 Selection Dock
docs.text: The Selection Dock shares the right-side dock area with the Command Panel. It collects selection kind, selection mode, picking mode, Show/Hide, and reset actions. Selection defines the target set for the next edit/delete/assign command; visibility is a separate render-view display state.

docs.title: 2.8.7 Output Window
docs.text: The Output Window is the bottom log area for execution results. It shows model import warnings, check-model results, analysis messages, and Remote Batch or Remote History status. When an action fails, start with the last message in the Output tab.

docs.title: 2.8.8 Node Table and Element Table
docs.text: Node Table and Element Table are table-style central views. They operate on the same model data as the create, update, and delete command families in the Node and Element menus. Edits made in a table follow the same Remote Control rules and history-recording behavior.

docs.title: 2.8.9 Chart View
docs.text: Chart View is a central view for plotting analysis results or signal-analysis results. It can be arranged as a tab or split like Render View. When multiple views are open, currentView and activeRenderView may be different.
